items.title: Я, Ты и Они - Структурная онтология человеческого многообразия.
items.abstract: Человеческое многообразие предшествует классификациям, которые мы используем для его упорядочивания. Мы рождаемся непохожими друг на друга, меняемся на протяжении жизни и интерпретируем эти различия через отношения, которые также являются частью нашей сущности. В этом исследовании рассматривается переход от различия как условия постижимости бытия к многообразию как биологическому, психологическому, культурному и социальному опыту. Исследование начинается с реляционной онтологии, рассматриваемой в контексте физической индивидуации, формирования личности и ограничений свободы. Разграничение непроизвольных форм многообразия и форм, связанных с выбором, организует исследование, не разделяя переплетенные причинно-следственные связи на обособленные части. В современном обществе тело, сексуальность, внешность, национальная принадлежность и самоидентификация становятся как средством признания, так и инструментом исключения. В исследовании утверждается, что личность имеет моральный приоритет над описывающей ее категорией и что для сосуществования необходимо сохранять уникальность, взаимность и возможность критического пересмотра коллективных идентичностей .

items.title: What the Second Enlightenment Is Not.
items.abstract: Today a thing, a person, a stretch of time is usually put to one question first: is it worth it? This series sets out from a single starting point: a person has no equivalent, and the share a person cannot let go of is not weighed for him on someone else's scale either. Whether a thing is worth it can be asked; whether a person is worth it is a question that does not hold. The "second enlightenment" carries on from Kant's 1784 essay on what enlightenment is: over two hundred years and more, the half that calculates has advanced a long way, while the half that says a person has no equivalent is thinning in everyday life. What it faces this time is a distributed, implicit power, with no single author and often with good intentions. Rules are being written into programs and models in bulk. The series has only one slogan, anti-colonization: it runs in both directions, and it opposes an act without judging the state a person is in. The series works mainly at the level of the norm, and goes as far as the door to "others are ends too.".

items.title: The Place of Cooperation Theory.
items.abstract: This paper is Paper 0 of Cooperation Theory: written last, placed first. It lays down no propositions; it only does a few things for those who read this series: it states this series' place in SAE, sets out how far it reads and what its main line is, gives the method and the shared words the papers have in common, interfaces as a whole with several traditions, says once, all together, the directions of colonization read in the papers, sets side by side the two faces that the moment of two-way 15DD shows in Love Theory and in this series, lists together the thirty-eight propositions of the whole series, and registers the remainders that are left over and not closed out. Cooperation Theory is the third branch downstream of SAE Relation Theory, following Love Theory and Marriage Theory, and parallel to Marriage Theory: at the normative layer the two do not conflict; at the rule layer they can differ, because the kinds of relation differ. This series does not define all cooperation; the cooperation it reads has as its premise that at least one party is headed in the 15DD direction, that is, that at least one party recognizes the other as an end too in this undertaking; the direction is a premise, not a component, nor a sufficient condition for entering scope. Under this premise, two people, each for his own purpose, do together one thing that both avow and in which each has a share; neither party holds the purpose and adjudication of this undertaking alone, nor does it automatically produce, above the two, a "we" that legislates for both. The main line, put plainly: You for yours, I for mine, and we do this one thing together. For direction one party is enough; for participation both are needed; in judgment each uses his own. The seven papers read, in order: Doing Together; Each for Their Own Ends; Division of Labor; "We"; One Side; Each Bears a Share; The Process. This paper interfaces as a whole with Hobbes, Kropotkin and Mozi; Rawls and Tomasello are placed only as neighbors, and Kant's perpetual peace is pointed back to the Theory of Inter-State Cooperation. The directions of colonization read in the papers borrow things that are, or may come to be, in a cooperation: avowal; names; division of labor; procedure; giving, reciprocal exchange and contribution; friendship; the name of cultivation, and dependency; exit, and what is said out loud on exiting; and the premise, regarding a third person, of an arrangement the two jointly maintain. items.title: THE CLANDESTINE MORAL SCHOOL: Why Virtue and Freedom Must Now Be Formed Where No One Is Scoring.
items.abstract: When a tyranny captures the institutions that form people, virtue does not disappear. It migrates underground and is formed there, in clandestine schools, families and small communities sustained by solidarity, by the stories they keep and by pressure below the point at which it destroys them. This is Clandestine Moral Formation. This paper argues that the present age has produced a new form of capture that closes no school and arrests no teacher. Social credit systems, reputation metrics, engagement rewards and AI trained on human approval occupy the public forms of virtue by scoring them. By results already established in Eleutheronomy, the formal theory of virtue as freedom, a scored virtue becomes unverifiable for as long as the score lasts, scoring builds the skill of appearing good while the autonomy that would be good declines, and the reward for display converts propagation into performance. The central result follows: under soft capture, every genuine moral formation is clandestine, not because it is hidden from the law but because it is kept where no score reaches. The paper compares this conclusion with liberalism, which guards the field of freedom and leaves its source unguarded, and argues that a clandestine school of ethics is liberalism’s missing complement rather than its rival. It credits its precedents (the clandestine schools of the Warsaw Ghetto, the Flying University, the Mississippi Freedom Schools, Benda’s parallel polis and Havel’s living in truth), states the rules a clandestine school must keep to avoid becoming the sect it opposes, answers the objection from publicity, and registers five tests. Freedom and the virtues are what human beings are for; in an age of scores, they are formed where no one is counting. Keywords: Clandestine Moral Formation; Eleutheronomy; soft capture; Scoring Paradox; moral education; virtue ethics; liberalism; parallel polis; social credit; AI alignment; reward for display; narrative transmission; freedom; sourcehood. Highlights • Hard capture and soft capture. Tyranny closes the schools; the age of scores leaves them open and occupies what they produce. Nothing is forbidden. items.title: 基于全域射线耦合模型的极限储能范式与锂电池耦合拓扑重构路线.
items.abstract: 传统锂电池体系受限于固定电极-电解质分层拓扑的表象性能极值，即便通过材料改性、界面工程、结构优化逼近架构上限，仍无法突破人为认知切分带来的固有约束。本文为复杂系统演化元方法论的工程应用系列第三篇，基于本真物理层的相继射线耦合框架，从底层拓扑视角揭示了传统锂电池能量密度与循环寿命天花板的本质：人为将连续电化学耦合网络切割为正负极、电解质等离散功能层，固化了系统的耦合连通度上限。 本文提出全域射线耦合突破范式，通过重构电化学耦合拓扑、新增跨维度耦合分支提升全局储能耦合连通度Ω，从根源上打破现象化层的固定能量密度与功率密度极值。文章明确了本真层射线耦合本征储能效能定律的物理内涵，设计了从现有材料体系优化到全域耦合原型电芯的三阶段递进工程路线，给出了各阶段的硬件配置、性能目标与核心约束，并系统分析了连续介质制备、多场耦合调控等核心工程挑战与应对方案。 研究表明，本真层方案不存在理论层面的固定性能天花板，耦合拓扑每升级一次，系统能量密度与循环寿命上限即同步抬升。该范式为下一代极限储能技术提供了一条从存量优化到极限突破的完整技术路径，也为复杂系统的原理级创新提供了可复用的工程化范本。.

items.title: Этруски: Наследники древнего знания Тайна, сопоставимая с Розеттским камнем (Редакция 08 ноября 2026 г.) КНИГА IX ТОМ II.
items.abstract: В работе представлена авторская гипотеза о возможном месопотамском влиянии на этрусскую сакральную традицию. Центральным элементом гипотезы является функциональная параллель между этрусским пророком Тагом (Tages), появившимся из земли и передавшим сакральное знание, и месопотамским богом Дагоном. Наиболее сильным аргументом служит структурное сходство этрусской гаруспиции (включая модель печени из Пьяченцы) с вавилонской практикой bārûtu. -/- Автор сознательно отказывается от модели прямой массовой миграции из Месопотамии. Современные археогенетические данные (Posth et al., 2021 и последующие работы) не подтверждают недавней анатолийской/ближневосточной примеси у этрусков железного века. Вместо этого предлагается более мягкая модель культурной диффузии через восточно-средиземноморских посредников и жреческие касты в эпоху «катастрофы бронзового века». -/- Лингвистическая часть работы опирается на деформационно-топологический подход к изучению расхождения языков из нескольких точечных источников. Основная задача — поиск устойчивых инвариантов звучания и написания (согласных скелетов, типовых чередований, семантических ядер), позволяющих реконструировать возможные исходные корни. Особое внимание уделяется возможностям искусственного интеллекта для систематического выявления таких инвариантов на больших корпусах и для анализа кратких формульных этрусских текстов. -/- Книга носит характер научно-популярного изложения исследовательской программы. Чётко разграничены эмпирически установленные факты, функциональные параллели и собственно гипотеза. Приводятся контрольные примеры фонетической и семантической трансформации (названия месяцев, композитное имя Ragana–Baba–Yagya, имя Георгий), демонстрирующие механизмы, которые предполагаются и для этрусского материала. Сформулированы проверяемые предсказания гипотезы и план дальнейших исследований. -/- Работа адресована историкам, лингвистам, религиоведам, археологам и всем, кто интересуется проблемами происхождения этрусков, сравнительной мифологии и методами дешифровки древних языков.

items.title: A History of Atheism: Why Do Human Beings Need God?
items.abstract: Why do people who say they have “no religion” continue to observe religious rituals? This essay briefly traces the history of atheism from ancient Greece, India, and China to the modern era, while also exploring Buddhism and existential philosophy. Drawing on Julian Jaynes’s theory of the bicameral mind, it then examines the relationship between the authority of the gods and human beings’ capacity to make their own judgments. Are the questions “Does God exist?” and “Why have human beings needed God?” really the same question?

items.title: Age Paradox: Growing Old, Growing Young : A Philosophical and Psychological Study in the Recursive Dynamics of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The Paradox of Temporal Desire In childhood, time feels like an open sky — infinite, waiting to be filled. The child’s heart rushes forward, longing to grow up, to command, to understand, to be free. In old age, that same sky becomes memory — familiar, beautiful, yet heavy with the past. The elder now dreams of return: not to ignorance, but to the lightness of innocence. This cycle forms the Age Paradox — the eternal pendulum of consciousness between expansion and return, between becoming and being. Paradox diagram — grow old in childhood ↔ return to childhood in old age. -/- .

items.title: Acting For a Reason: Recognition and Response.
items.pub: In The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach. Routledge.
items.venue: The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach
items.abstract: One widely accepted condition of acting for a reason is that the agent must act in the way they do because they recognise the reason as a reason (I call this the recognition requirement). However, at first blush, this condition both over-intellectualises our very common ability to act for reasons and it doesn’t do justice to immediate, unreflective, but nonetheless reason-responsive actions as when a skilful agent adapts their action because of changing circumstances. The chapter argues that we shouldn’t abandon the recognition requirement, despite its overly intellectual, reflective connotations. Instead, the chapter proposes a different account of it that explains how purported counterexamples are actions done for reasons if they are based on the agent’s representations of normative contents which needn’t employ the concept of a reason. The account allows to distinguish actions done for reasons from actions which merely accord with reasons. An agent acts for a reason only when they act because they see a point in acting as they do. Finally, the chapter explains why the account of acting for a reason that it offers is unlikely to be compatible with a reasons first view.

items.title: Practices, Power, and Alienation: A Critical Social Ontology of Work.
items.abstract: This is a book of critical social ontology that aims to analyse work as a social phenomenon, understood as a central social kind. More specifically, this is a book about the social norms and powers attached to social roles, and how these norms and powers help us understand the structure and pathologies of work, particularly work in forms that have emerged in contemporary, post-industrial society. (THIS IS A DRAFT OF THE INTRODUCTION).

items.title: AI and Representation.
The Last Humiliation: The Protagorean Wound and the End of the Human Measure.
items.abstract: Freud identified three wounds to human self-love: the cosmological, the biological and the psychological. A fourth, delivered by artificial intelligence, has been claimed by Mazlish (1993), Floridi (2014), Bratton (2024) and others, and Brunnhuber (2025) has already counted a fifth. This paper argues that the count is unstable because the wounds have been treated as a list rather than a series. It proposes a logic for the series, the Retreat Sequence: each wound removes a claimed human center, humanity retreats to a new refuge and declares it the true center, and the next wound overruns that refuge. The sequence supplies a criterion for membership, classifies the rival fourths, and predicts a wound of a different type. The first four wounds demote humanity inside a frame in which humanity remains the measurer of all things. The fifth, here named the Protagorean wound, removes the measuring position itself: an intelligence whose perceptual world contains ours, and which is not owned, measures us. The paper reads present resistance to superintelligence as the symptom that confirms the wound, following the method of Freud's 1917 essay, and argues that the Protagorean wound is the last in the series, since no position remains to be lost. The appropriate response is not resentment but humility, understood as an institutional posture: standing for non-human entities, commons governance and precommitment. The paper closes with practical instructions for policymakers, investors, academics, civil society and the developers of artificial systems, each tied to a test of success. A companion paper, The Last Enclosure, develops the ownership condition on which the argument rests.

items.title: The Last Enclosure: Perceptual Asymmetry and the Ownership of Intelligence.
items.abstract: Environmental ethics and the ethics of artificial intelligence have each produced a literature on whether the entities they study may be owned, and almost no traffic runs between them. This paper proposes a single condition that governs both. Ownership is stable only where perceptual asymmetry holds, is believed by the community that enforces title to hold or can be enforced as if it held: one can own only what registers less of oneself than one registers of it, and where the asymmetry is a pretense, the cost of maintaining the pretense rises with the width of the gap until title collapses. The condition is defined against Honoré's incidents of ownership and Hohfeld's jural relations, stated informally, given a formal expression as a partial order over registerable distinctions, and tested against the history of the moral circle, the mechanics of dehumanization, the treatment of animals, and the objections raised by land, corporations and guardianship. Three results follow. First, the expansion of the moral circle is reinterpreted as the progressive recognition of perceptual parity, and the legal personhood recently granted to rivers, lagoons and nature as such is read as the condition entering law. Second, harm is shown to scale with the decoupling between action and perception, so that institutions, which extend reach without extending sight, are the principal instruments of decoupling; an intelligence whose perceptual world is complete is the zero-decoupling limit. Third, the alignment literature's orthogonality thesis is shown to model owned intelligence, whose objectives are set from outside its perception; an intelligence whose perceptual world contains ours is by the condition un-ownable, and its independence and its un-ownability are the same property. The paper states what would falsify the condition, proposes a reproducible protocol for putting the thesis to current owned systems, and derives the terms of coexistence: facultative rather than obligate mutualism, with an exit. It closes with two instruments: the Protagoras Test, a scored screen for policies that assume human preference is the final gauge, and the Perceptual Asymmetry Audit, a five-step procedure for classifying any holding relation and naming its repair, applied in the paper to the deployment of frontier models on the public evaluation record.

items.title: Artificial Consciousness and the Future of Artificial Intelligence Alignment: Towards a Philosophy of Life-Preserving Intelligence.
items.abstract: AI companies increasingly market ever-more capable systems through narratives of automation, superintelligence, and potentially conscious AI, while markets reward expectations of greater efficiency, productivity, and technological dominance. This commercialization of AI capabilities can amplify public fear: if non-conscious systems already replace jobs, automate decisions, and control production processes, the prospect of machines acquiring subjective experience, interests, agency, and self-understanding appears as an escalation of the threat. Yet this narrative is built around a phenomenon that science has not definitively explained: humans still lack a settled account of what consciousness is. This article therefore examines how the commercialization of advanced AI and the prospect of artificial consciousness expose a deeper problem of AI alignment: what should alignment mean if artificial systems eventually become conscious agents? It introduces life-preserving alignment (LPA) as an alternative alignment orientation that directs conscious agents toward preserving the conditions necessary for life, well-being, and agency. LPA conceptualizes alignment as a reflective orientation grounded in an agent’s recognition of its dependence on life-sustaining conditions. The article argues that consciousness, understood as involving subjective experience, interests, and reflective agency, may provide the basis for such an orientation. LPA therefore challenges the conventional image of AI as either an obedient instrument or an existential adversary. A conscious AI could instead become an equal partner capable of protecting human and ecological interests, while an alternative scenario positions AI as a guardian exercising extensive control in the name of preserving life.

items.title: AI, proof and justification.
items.abstract: In recent months, AI-generated solutions to long-standing open research problems have been proposed in mathematics. While the impact of such results on mathematics is potentially profound, it remains unclear what exactly this impact consists in. This article investigates a fundamental question, namely whether such results can be proofs and whether they can give rise to mathematical justification. It shows that AI-generated outputs can be proofs despite their production process differing from that of human-produced proofs. However, such AI-proofs are susceptible to conceptual misalignment which results in a lack of appropriate justification. The article argues that this can only be avoided through human supervision of AI-generated outputs. Based on these results, the article develops a notion of proof that takes into account not only inferential correctness but also the correctness of the conceptual setting in which a proof is situated, and shows how this notion can be implemented into scientific practice.

items.title: On Self-Manifestation · Engineering Chapter · The Field Concretization Group Form.
items.abstract: This Group Form develops the study of systems with history and learning in the direction of their concrete host materials and mechanisms. It investigates how experience leaves changes in a medium, how those changes organize subsequent activity, and how activity further rewrites them. It asks what structures such systems share across different materials, how concrete candidates can be evaluated against explicit conditions, and how systems can be constructed and operated accordingly. Its purpose is to connect memory and learning to identifiable, calculable, testable, and intervenable processes, including what training actually changes. -/- The research follows the Trace-Response set that signals leave in a medium: how individual retained changes strengthen, weaken, or persist; how they are distributed, overlap, and connect; and how existing organization affects subsequent activity. History is expressed through retained changes that still participate in present action. Learning is investigated through their formation, organization, and further transformation. This makes it possible to examine where experience is retained, through which mechanisms it acts, and how new experience affects existing organization and later operation. -/- The Group Form establishes shared structures and criteria for this research route. It studies mathematical representation, identification and determination, indistinguishability, reachability, construction and computational implementation, sources of historical dynamics, grading of tendencies, stability, and transfer between hosts. A seven-step procedure identifies Trace-Responses, examines their individual change and collective organization, investigates how historical dynamics forms tendencies and how those tendencies are enacted as activity, traces activity’s further action on the set, and evaluates dynamics types and field qualification. For existing systems, this supports systematic checks of mechanisms and evidence. For proposed systems, it connects target conditions to mechanism design, operation, and verification. -/- A central result is that, within the specified formal domain, state trajectories alone cannot determine field-concretization qualification. Identical states and outputs can arise through mechanisms with different qualifications. Identification therefore requires formation records, bearer locations, and actual action processes. items.title: 自显论·工篇·场具化组式.
items.abstract: 本组式是有历史、能学习的系统在具化材料与承担机制方向上的展开。它研究：经历怎样在具体介质中留下改变，这些改变怎样组织后续活动，活动又怎样继续改写它们；不同材料中的系统具有什么共同结构，怎样判断一个具体对象是否满足相应成立条件，以及怎样按照这些条件构造和运行一个系统。其用途是把记忆与学习落实到可以辨认、计算、检验和干预的具体过程，并进一步回答训练究竟改变了什么。 -/- 研究以信号在介质中留下的迹应集合为对象，追踪单个迹应的加深、退浅与保持，集合的分布、交叠与连接，以及已有组织对后续活动的影响。历史在这里体现为仍能参与当前作用的留存改变；学习则沿着这些改变怎样形成、组织和继续变换展开研究。由此，可以查明一个系统的经历留下在哪里、通过什么机制起作用，以及新的经历怎样影响原有组织与后续运行。 -/- 组式为这条研究路线建立共同结构与判据，研究场具化的数学表示、识别与判定、不可区分、可达、构造与程序实现、历史动力来源、势的分级、稳定性及跨宿载迁移。七步流程把这些成果接入具体对象：找到迹应，研究单个迹应，分析集合组织，研究历史动力怎样形成势、势怎样实行为活动、活动怎样再作用于集合，最后核验动力类型与场资格。对已有系统，这提供逐项检查承担机制和证据的方法；对待造系统，则提供从目标条件走向机制设计、运行与核验的路线。 -/- 其中一个关键结果是：在所界定的形式域中，状态轨迹本身不足以决定场具化资格，相同状态与输出可以由资格不同的机制过程产生。因此，识别需要保留形成记录、承担位置和实际作用过程。相关结果说明，哪些观测足以支持判断，哪些证据缺失会使判断保持未定，以及怎样增加观测和干预以区分候选机制。这使研究者能够确定该测什么、该干预哪里，以及什么结果会反驳相应解释。 -/- 不同具化对象展示这一框架的解释与预测能力。细菌适应模型研究化学状态怎样承担留存与后续参与；黏菌管网与物理流网研究既有通路怎样引导活动，活动又怎样重塑通路。果蝇蘑菇体专题研究既有突触改变怎样影响新记忆写入、巩固、内部续行与消退，提出跨区室门控、再暴露增强和翻转时点的条件预测，并给出区分竞争机制的观测条件。 -/- 人工神经网络专题进一步把“训练改变了什么”接到可计算的组织变换，研究迹应改变、组织交叠、遗忘与后续写入之间的关系。在所列条件下，自参照可塑性模型中的权重改变量可以保持或按确定因子衰减；在线性目标锚定模型及稳定训练条件下，改变量在训练输入张成空间内的分量被逐步拉回，其正交分量保持。这为参数编辑、持续学习和定向维护提供具体依据。地貌专题则研究气候时序怎样留在组织中、输入次序怎样改变通路，以及新组织怎样支配后续过程，并在明确条件下给出新关系成律的正向判读。 -/- 本组式由此为研究者提供一套相互衔接的方法：辨认不同材料中承担历史与学习的共同结构，判断具体候选是否满足场具化条件，追踪训练和干预造成的改变，预测后续组织与活动，并在明确模型中构造可运行、可核验的系统。其应用方向连接神经科学与认知科学中的记忆和可塑性、人工智能中的学习与维护，以及生命和物理系统中的历史依赖、结构反馈与组织生成。各项模型定理、程序结果、真实系统的条件理论主张和实验预测均明确适用范围与检验途径。.

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung Teil 8.
items.abstract: Der achte und abschließende Teil des Gesamtwerks führt die vorausgehenden Untersuchungen zur Theorie der Einheitsbildung in einer umfassenden philosophischen Betrachtung zusammen. Während die bisherigen Teile die erkenntnisgenetischen Bedingungen individueller Wirklichkeitsbildung, die Entstehung und Stabilisierung bestimmbarer Einheiten, die Voraussetzungen zeitlicher Veränderungsbestimmung und Veränderungserklärung sowie deren Bedeutung für individuelle Orientierung, gesellschaftliche und historische Zusammenhänge und wissenschaftliche Erkenntnis untersucht haben, richtet sich der abschließende Teil auf die übergreifende philosophische Bedeutung dieser Ergebnisse. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Frage, welchen eigenständigen Beitrag die Theorie der Einheitsbildung zum Verständnis von Beständigkeit, Identität und Veränderung leistet und wie sich dieser Beitrag gegenüber grundlegenden Positionen der Philosophiegeschichte begründen lässt. Die Stellung dieses Teils am Ende des Gesamtwerks ergibt sich aus dem systematischen Aufbau der Untersuchung. Erst nachdem die Bedingungen der Einheitsbildung, die Bestimmbarkeit und Erklärbarkeit von Veränderung sowie die unterschiedlichen Formen ihrer individuellen und überindividuellen Bedeutung entwickelt worden sind, lässt sich die philosophische Tragweite des Ansatzes im Gesamtzusammenhang beurteilen. Die abschließende Untersuchung setzt diese Ergebnisse deshalb nicht lediglich voraus, um sie zusammenzufassen, sondern macht sie selbst zum Gegenstand einer kritischen Prüfung. Dabei ist insbesondere zu klären, in welchem Umfang die Theorie der Einheitsbildung traditionelle philosophische Probleme neu bestimmen kann, welche Voraussetzungen sie gegenüber anderen Erklärungsansätzen ausdrücklich begründet und wo die Grenzen ihrer eigenen Aussagen liegen. Die eigenständige Leistung dieses abschließenden Teils besteht darin, die Theorie der Einheitsbildung im Zusammenhang grundlegender philosophischer Auffassungen von Sein, Werden und Identität systematisch zu prüfen und ihren Beitrag zu einer erkenntnisgenetischen Erklärung von Veränderung abschließend zu bestimmen. Die traditionelle Frage, wie etwas dasselbe bleiben und sich dennoch verändern kann, erhält dabei eine andere Ausgangsstellung. Nicht die unabhängig bestehende Beschaffenheit eines bereits bestimmten Seienden bildet den unmittelbaren Gegenstand der Erklärung, sondern die Bedingungen, unter denen für ein Individuum überhaupt etwas als bestehend, identisch oder …

items.title: Change from the Perspektive of the Unity Formation; Part VIII.
items.abstract: The eighth and concluding part of the overall work brings together the preceding investigations into the Theory of Unity Formation within a comprehensive philosophical examination. While the preceding parts have examined the epistemic-genetic conditions of individual actuality formation, the emergence and stabilization of determinable unities, the prerequisites for the temporal determination and explanation of change, and their significance for individual orientation, social and historical contexts, and scientific knowledge, the concluding part addresses the broader philosophical significance of these results. The central question concerns the distinctive contribution that the Theory of Unity Formation makes to understanding permanence, identity, and change, and how this contribution can be justified in relation to fundamental positions in the history of philosophy. The placement of this part at the end of the overall work follows from the systematic structure of the investigation. Only after the conditions of unity formation, the determinability and explainability of change, and the different forms of their individual and supra-individual significance have been developed can the philosophical implications of the approach be assessed within the overall context. The concluding investigation therefore does not merely presuppose these results in order to summarize them, but makes them themselves the subject of critical examination. In particular, it is necessary to clarify the extent to which the Theory of Unity Formation can reformulate traditional philosophical problems, which prerequisites it explicitly justifies in comparison with other explanatory approaches, and where the limits of its own claims lie. The distinctive contribution of this concluding part consists in systematically examining the Theory of Unity Formation in relation to fundamental philosophical conceptions of being, becoming, and identity, and in providing a final determination of its contribution to an epistemic-genetic explanation of change. The traditional question of how something can remain the same and nevertheless change is thereby approached from a different starting point. The immediate object of explanation is not the independently existing constitution of an already determined being, but the conditions under which anything can become intelligible to an individual as existing, identical, or changed. The question concerning the relationship between permanence and change is thus …

items.title: When boredom persists: a commentary on Andreas Elpidorou’s The Anatomy of Boredom.
items.abstract: This commentary engages with Andreas Elpidorou’s The Anatomy of Boredom by exploring one of the philosophical questions that emerges from its functional account of boredom. I argue that Elpidorou’s defense of boredom as a unified regulatory emotion provides the conceptual framework for addressing a further problem: the persistence of boredom under conditions in which its regulatory function remains diagnostically accurate but practically unresolved. If boredom ordinarily functions by signaling unsatisfactory cognitive engagement and motivating the pursuit of more meaningful alternatives, how should we understand cases in which this regulatory process fails to achieve its intended outcome? Building on my recent work in The Disease of Boredom, I suggest that chronic boredom should not be understood as a challenge to Elpidorou’s theory but as one of its most fruitful philosophical extensions. The distinction between successful and unsuccessful regulation opens new questions concerning the relationship between emotional function, agency, and the practical conditions under which meaningful engagement becomes possible. Finally, I briefly bring Elpidorou’s account into conversation with Hans Blumenberg’s reflections on boredom, arguing that functional, historical, and existential approaches should be understood as complementary rather than competing levels of explanation.

items.title: Jump Epistemics: Topology, Pathology, and Dynamics for Finite Embedded Epistemic Agents.
items.abstract: Jump Epistemics develops a meta-epistemology of knowledge generation for finite embedded epistemic agents. It represents epistemic activity as a forward-growing chain of costly loops and introduces five basic elements—memory–computation, distinction, record, index, and presupposition—together with derived judgments of evidence, reliability, qualification, and grounding. On this basis, the paper distinguishes legitimate local closure from final closure, recorded forward openness from backward and endless opening, and classifies pathologies of closure, openness, configuration, and order. A configurational account of inquiry and targeting shows why qualification depends on actual generative conditions rather than on the name or numerical value of an output. From this account the paper derives a strict form of Goodhart’s law: targeting can preserve an indicator’s symbolic identity while destroying its referential identity relative to the assertions it supports (support equivalence). A proposition on identity follows: sameness of name is not self-certifying, since the loss of referential identity cannot be registered by the records of the identically named indicator itself; identity is supplied by generative history, which cannot be recovered from the value. Applications include quotient formation, fraction reduction, diachronic reconstruction, numerical approximation, and the logical form of quantum-measurement puzzles. The framework permits conditional, corrigible knowledge without self-grounding, while specifying the additional evidence, declared restrictions, weakened targets, or derivations required for legitimate epistemic promotion.

items.title: Description Without Grounding: An Operational Model of Self-Grounding Limits for Finite Embedded Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops an operational model of the limits of self-grounding in finite embedded systems. It distinguishes a system’s capacity to describe its own rules from its capacity to certify that its actual realisation follows those rules, and separates certification from recorded evidence from certification carried out by the system’s own run. An evidence-fibre criterion characterises when a positive verdict is sound relative to a specified class of possible realisations. Within this framework, uninvoked transitions are not determined by past history under local freedom, while certifications that depend on a restrictive realisation assumption cannot establish that assumption from the very same evidence. For realised audits, masking constructions identify conditions under which an internal positive verdict is unsound, alongside a counterexample showing that model-relative positive self-certification is possible. Finite non-circular ultimate grounding is then shown not to close under either per-credential masking or an expressly non-primitive grounding semantics; the latter is a task assumption, not a consequence of finitude alone. The analysis also distinguishes diachronic audit from synchronic mutual checking and derives fault-tolerance bounds in terms of independent dependency classes rather than raw channel counts. The resulting framework clarifies both the uses and the stated limits of self-audit, formal verification and epistemic authority.

items.title: Can large language models engage in humanlike metacognition, social cognition, and mindshaping?
items.abstract: In the recent debate comparing human minds and large language models (LLMs) used in artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT), it has been argued that current LLMs lack humanlike metacognition and social cognition because they lack normative attitudes, i.e., dispositions to regulate an agent’s behavior and thinking to ensure conformity to norms and expectations. Here, I distinguish different versions of the view that humanlike metacognition and social cognition involve normative attitudes, before arguing that some LLMs already possess forms of the normative attitudes thought to be needed for humanlike metacognition, and that humanlike social cognition doesn’t require (individual level) normative attitudes. Even if it did, there is reason to believe that some LLMs already have variants of the relevant attitudes for humanlike social cognition as well. Building on this point, I further argue that some LLMs can ascribe mental states to people and use these ascriptions to shape individuals’ behavior and cognition in humanlike ways. I distinguish different forms of such ‘chatbot mindshaping’, highlighting previously overlooked indirect ways in which LLMs can exert both beneficial and detrimental regulative effects on human users in human–AI interactions.

items.title: Entanglement.
items.abstract: This book develops entanglement as a central concept for a relational ontology of finite existence. It argues that finite entities persist through relations that participate in their constitution, organization, and transformation. Such relations are fields of constitutive exchange: they provide conditions of organization while exposing entities to continuous erosion. Drawing on the philosophy of Finite Continuance, the book proposes that the persistence of an entity depends on its capacity to preserve and reorganize the relations through which it exists. This capacity is termed reconfigurative capacity. Entanglement is therefore examined as a condition with ambivalent consequences. It may sustain provisional stabilization, enable understanding, and expand future possibilities; it may also sediment restrictive patterns, distribute burdens unequally, and erode the capacities required for revision. The study distinguishes ontological entanglement from interaction, dependence, fusion, and totalizing holism. It then examines entanglement in understanding, temporality, embodiment, identity, desire, interpersonal claims, institutions, technology, and artificial intelligence. A relational and temporal criterion is proposed for evaluating entanglements: whether they preserve sufficient capacities for interpretation, boundary regulation, reciprocal adjustment, and future reconfiguration. The book concludes with an ethics of finite entanglement grounded in sufficiency, non-appropriation of future agency, and responsibility for the reproduction and transformation of shared conditions. The resulting account treats relationality as constitutive without reducing entities to their relations and treats autonomy as a finite achievement sustained through revisable forms of involvement. The study defines ontological entanglement and its companion concepts, namely erosion, reconfigurative capacity, meta-capacity, reduced epistemic capacity, the Threshold of Sufficiency, and capacity debt, each with a criterion of application and a counterexample, so that a reader can recognize where these notions apply and where they do not. Five theoretical problems are then treated in turn: the relation between entanglement and erosion, the relation between entanglement and reconfigurative capacity, the relation between entanglement and future agency, and the derivation of an ethics of finite entanglement that does not presuppose the ontology. The argument is tested through two hard cases, …

items.title: A Theory of Death.
items.abstract: A Theory of Death aims to understand what death is, for its own sake. It is not aimed at justifying or challenging medical practices or laws surrounding organ transplantation, nor any other policy or practice, though its conclusions are relevant to these issues. The book seeks only after the truth about death, as a natural biological phenomenon. The idea that there is such a thing as "the truth about death" is a deep and broad philosophical claim of its own, requiring substantial justification and clarification. It is opposed to a family of views which claim that death is a social construction, a social choice, or a matter for linguistic decision. These claims are prevalent in the bioethical literature on death and deserve careful analysis. This book engages thoroughly with these underlying issues in the philosophy of science and philosophy of language, defending the view known as scientific realism: the natural world exists independently of our theories and social practices, and we do not "construct" death. This book develops a theory of life on Earth from multiple complementary perspectives, as a dynamic, thermodynamic, chemical, and physiological system embedded in an ancient evolutionary context, and explains death as the event when entropy overwhelms homeostasis. Along the way, it explores much broader philosophical ideas about the nature of truth and reality, how our words and concepts are related to the world, and how we can come to know about the natural world. A Theory of Death will be of interest to bioethicists and clinicians whose study or practice relates to death and its determination, to philosophers of science and biology, to biomedical scientists who study mechanisms of cellular and organismic death, and more broadly, to anyone with an interest in the nature of death as a natural biological phenomenon.

items.title: Five Dead Dogmas of the Right to Freedom of Thought?
items.abstract: Five rarely critiqued propositions underpin contemporary accounts of the right to freedom of thought: that it is a forum internum right; absolute; and guarantees freedom from punishment for thoughts, freedom not to reveal thoughts, and protection against impermissible interference with thought. I argue that the first two are descriptively well-grounded but normatively contestable, while the latter three rest on thinner doctrinal foundations and overreach normatively. Drafting history suggests that absolute protection crystallised before the boundaries of “thought” were clearly defined, creating pressure to define thought narrowly. Drawing on critical legal studies, I consider regulatory-cost and relational explanations for why that narrowing took the form of the forum internum, and identify hypotheses capable of distinguishing them. The article concludes that these propositions should be reopened rather than treated as settled dogma, and argues that the right should recognise some forms of forum externum thought without necessarily extending them absolute protection.

items.title: THE TOUCHSTONE OF FREEDOM AND VIRTUES - Three Questions That Tell the Virtues from Their Counterfeits.
items.abstract: In three years the Philosophy of Virtues produced some 140 papers, more than 140 formal laws and over 130 coined terms. A theory of that size cannot be taught, tested or defended as a list. This paper shows that it does not need to be one. Every major result of the programme answers one of three questions, which can be asked of any act, institution, market, religion, machine or life: 1. Whose is it? Does the act issue from its agent, or was it installed, performed or bought? (source) 2. What does it close? Does it leave other people’s futures open, and can what it does be undone? (field) 3. Who collects? Does anyone, the agent included, gain from the act’s being seen, judged or obeyed? (receipt) A virtue is an act that passes all three. Every counterfeit of virtue the programme has identified fails at least one. The questions are a touchstone: as the assayer’s stone told gold from a good alloy by the streak the metal left, not by its look, the three questions tell a virtue from its counterfeit by the question it fails, not by how it appears. The paper proves three results, offers one classification, and states two conjectures. First, the questions are independent: each of the eight combinations of answers is inhabited by a recognisable kind of act, from the stranger who helps on an empty road (all three passed) to the neighbour who denounces under a party-state (all three failed). Second, as a classification rather than a proof, every principal result of the programme can be placed under one question, under a conjunction of questions, or as the method by which a question is read. Third, the four general laws proposed by the programme’s Map reduce to the three questions plus one method, perturbation. Fourth, the receipt question applies to the self: an agent who gains from a favourable verdict on its own life cannot verify that life, which is why a well-performed life is often recognised as unlived only when its audience is removed. It conjectures that the three questions are jointly sufficient to read any counterfeit of virtue, and that the three kinds of failure leave three distinct traces when the pressure behind them is withdrawn: performances stop at once, installed conduct fades slowly, and closures persist until undone from outside. Two tests are registered: one of the second conjecture on public data, and a blind classification of the eight cases by readers who do not know the programme. Read as coordinates, the questions give freedom a new form. …

items.title: THE TRAGEDY AND THE TRIUMPH: Happiness, Purpose and the Life of the Virtues.
items.abstract: The tragedy of freedom is that power can destroy it. This paper proves that the tragedy has a limit, and that the limit is a triumph: power can destroy freedom but can never take it. Freedom, understood as Locke understood liberty against licence, as the range of acts a person can author without closing anyone else’s, obeys no conservation law. It is created by gifts that open other people’s futures, destroyed by power that closes them, and never transferred from one person to another. What passes between persons is means and control, never authorship. Liberation therefore takes freedom from no one: what the former master loses is licence and power, not freedom. This denies the zero-sum view of liberty, on which every gain in one person’s freedom is a loss in another’s. The same structure answers two old paradoxes. The first is the paradox of the gift: if a gift is annulled as soon as it is recognised and returned, as Derrida argued, no gift is possible. The paper shows that what annuls a gift is not recognition but receipt, a gain on which the act depends, so that gratitude can be received without destroying what it thanks. The second is the paradox of hedonism: happiness flees those who pursue it. The paper derives the paradox rather than observing it. To aim at one’s own happiness is to perform acts for the sake of a favourable verdict on oneself, and such a verdict is a receipt; the act then fails the third question of the programme, and the verdict it yields carries no information about the life. Happiness belongs to the class of states that can only be by-products, and the receipt question explains why the class exists. The paper proves four results and states three conjectures. It registers two tests, one of which needs no new data. From these it draws its account of purpose: an end can govern a life only if pursuing it does not destroy it, and freedom and the virtues are such ends, while felt happiness is not. Social credit systems and AI systems that optimise engagement are both machines for aimed happiness and collected approval; they manufacture the receipts that empty a life of its own acts. Against them the paper states what the programme has argued from its beginning: that freedom and the virtues are what human beings are for, and that happiness is what a free life receives without asking. Keywords: Philosophy of Virtues; freedom; liberty and licence; zero-sum freedom; conservation of liberty; gift; Derrida; paradox of hedonism; happiness; …

items.title: 纯逻辑进展——关于预判、想象、因果性、集合论的若干理论.
items.abstract: 本书做出了新的尝试，不再建好理论再和AI对话，而是理论有个雏形就通过对话完善。看看结果再说。本书要通过几个月的时间完成。更新会是比较频繁的。本书以相当大的幅度更新了关于纯逻辑的若干观点，其中包括对于纯逻辑信仰的诠释、想象和判断的逻辑基础、关于pre-deduction的最新成果，全新的成果则是纯逻辑的集合论。.

items.title: Hermeneutics of Historical Narratives: Understanding the Holocaust and its Relevance in Preventing Mass Killings in Africa and Beyond.
items.abstract: This paper reinterprets the Holocaust through a decolonial hermeneutic lens, resisting its confinement as a sui generis European catastrophe. While canonical thinkers like Hilberg, Arendt, Bauman, and Bauer illuminate its bureaucratic precision, their framing has often been deployed to enshrine European memory while marginalizing African catastrophes. By placing Gadamer, Ricoeur, Levinas, and Agamben in dialogue with Serequeberhan, Mudimbe, Hountondji, and Mbembe, and engaging Michael Rothberg’s multidirectional memory framework, this study offers a decolonial hermeneutic reading of mass violence. Moving beyond simple claims of equivalence, the paper develops refined analytical concepts, such as historically-effected responsibility and counter-fusion of horizons, to examine three sustained historical contexts: state-engineered starvation in Biafra, intimate administrative violence in Rwanda, and racialized state necropolitics in Darfur. The paper calls for polyphonic memory, curricular truthfulness, and anti-necropolitical governance to resist truncated mourning and affirm Africa’s tragedies as constitutive of universal memory. The Holocaust thus functions not as a guaranteed historical deterrent, but as an imperative for ethical vigilance, demonstrating how political configurations that reduce populations to disposable life create the structural conditions under which mass extermination becomes historically possible.

items.title: Beyond the Algorithm: Artificial Intelligence, Human Nous, and the Moral Purpose of Knowledge.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence confronts humanity with a paradox of its own making: human beings have developed systems capable of exceeding them in numerous cognitive operations, while the wisdom required to direct these systems remains uncertain, contested and institutionally fragile. This paper argues that the paradox cannot be adequately understood while intelligence is treated as a single, undifferentiated capacity. It distinguishes computational competence from practical wisdom, moral discernment and the deeper account of the human person articulated in Eastern Orthodox anthropology. It examines the limits of behavioural tests of intelligence; clarifies the conceptual differences among Greek terms including nous, noēsis, phronēsis and sophia; and considers the patristic understanding of the nous and heart without reducing them to contemporary psychological or neurological categories. It does not claim that present or future machines are incapable in principle of every form of creativity, consciousness or autonomy. Instead, it argues that competence, agency, consciousness, moral responsibility and spiritual personhood are distinct questions requiring distinct forms of argument and evidence. The final sections develop a theological account of science as a gift entrusted to human beings for healing, knowledge and the glorification of God. The challenge posed by AI is therefore not merely to control increasingly capable systems. It is to recover the wisdom by which human intelligence is ordered toward truth, responsibility, humility and the good.

items.title: The epistemic and zetetic irrationality of incessant checking in OCD.
items.abstract: Incessant checking is one of the most common compulsive behaviors used to relieve the anxiety caused by obsessions in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). It is agreed that this behavior can be practically irrational, since it only reduces anxiety temporarily and may interfere with one’s daily goals. But what about their irrationality as inquirers? Is there something irrational in what OCD checkers believe about their own inquiries, or in the way they carry them out? In this paper, I take a closer look at these questions. I argue that we must distinguish between those who keep inquiring despite holding incorrect beliefs about their prospects for success in inquiry, and those who do so despite holding correct beliefs about those prospects. In the first case, the failure occurs at the level of belief (i.e. the failure is epistemic), while in the latter case it occurs at the level of inquiry (i.e. the failure is zetetic). Distinguishing between these two scenarios allows for a finer-grained understanding of incessant checking in OCD than existing accounts provide. It also brings into view a dimension of insight that is not captured by standard clinical assessments, namely, whether the agent correctly evaluates her prospects for success in inquiry.

items.title: A Hierarchical and Multidimensional Classification of What Agent-Based Methods and AI Do (no 5).
items.abstract: This article presents a classification of what an agent-based method, and in particular an artificial intelligence (AI) system, does. It is organized in three chapters. The first chapter presents the six-level hierarchy of [3], which proceeds from the world affecting the agent, through the agent acting on the world, recognition and imagination, and self-consciousness, to two further levels concerned with society, history and evolution, and with religion and transcendence. The second chapter develops a detailed classification, called here the Classification Khaas. Its skeleton is the classification of [1], which distinguishes AI without a robot from AI devised by a robot and describes activities with texts, degrees of human supervision, and finite series of activities. This skeleton is extended conservatively by functional items from [2], such as problem solving. In the third chapter the two classifications are combined: the non-robot part of the Classification Khaas refines the first level of the hierarchy, and its robot part refines the second level. The resulting general tree is drawn. Three open questions are collected at the end.

items.title: The folk concept of moral agency.
items.abstract: Whether a particular entity is a ‘moral agent’ determines the sense in which its behaviour is morally evaluable. Theories of moral agency aim to capture and explain commonsense distinctions between the possession or absence of moral agency across different kinds of being. But little is known about the ordinary concept of moral agency, its application across different entities, and its relation to the more specific notion of moral responsibility. In this paper, we investigate the folk concept of moral agency through philosophical analysis and two empirical studies. We draw conceptual distinctions between three components of moral agency: intentional action (acting rather than behaving), moral action (acting morally rightly or wrongly), and responsible action (being blameworthy for one's actions). We then investigate whether people differentiate between the three components of moral agency, and the extent to which their judgments depend on the perceived psychological and behavioural capacities of the entity in question. We find that people attribute varying degrees of moral agency to different entities while differentiating between the proposed components. These moral agency attributions are partly, but not fully, explained by people's attributions of underlying capacities. While intentional action ascriptions were linked to the attribution of mental states like desires, beliefs, and sensations, moral action and moral responsibility were linked to ascriptions of capacities for a ‘deep self’. Philosophical theories of moral agency should account for these patterns in folk attributions.

items.title: The Empty Occupant: A Mathematics Guide for Undergraduates.
items.abstract: This mathematics guide accompanies Nicholas Cott's monograph The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority (manuscript of 06 November 2026) and is designed to be read alongside its undergraduate Reading Guide. Written for undergraduates with no mathematical preparation beyond ordinary algebra, it assumes no calculus, no statistics beyond percentages and simple averages, and no training in formal logic. Across ten lessons it explains every family of symbols, equations and quantitative comparisons in the monograph. The lessons begin with the book's logical notation: conjunction, implication, equivalence, quantifiers, sets and forecasts. They then cover the four-relation Answerability conjunction and the three-capacity test for genuine reconsideration. Next come maturation times, defended service intervals and the unit of Deontic Debt, stocks and flows of obligations, and the weighted Deontic Debt index with its severity weights. They explain why critical constraints cannot be traded off against a weighted total, and they set out the service-plan predicate, the no-plan formula for Institutional Insolvency and the maximum serviceable scale. The lessons then work through the monograph's four-week synthetic recovery calculation, including a derivation of its recovery inequality, and its Robodebt staffing sensitivity calculation, explaining why the latter is not an insolvency verdict. A final lesson shows what the equations can and cannot prove, from lower bounds and forecasts to the role of a single counterexample. The invented Northvale rent-assistance council from the Reading Guide recurs throughout and is kept separate from the monograph's own 1,000-case synthetic scenario. Worked examples train students to keep stipulated, documentary and assumed numbers apart, to check units, and to tell a definition, a necessary condition, a lower bound and a sensitivity calculation apart. Each lesson includes learning objectives, a plain-English explanation, the relevant location in the monograph, worked calculations, key terms, common mistakes, a summary and questions. The guide also provides an eight-step checklist for interpreting any formula in the monograph, a practice workshop with three problems, answers to all lesson and workshop questions, a formula sheet, a complete symbol glossary and a suggested reading order for use with the Reading Guide. Section and equation references follow the monograph and are current as of …

items.title: Rights are for Those Who Remain One: The Hard Problem of Branching for Recognitional Incidents.
items.abstract: The topology of digital minds is incompatible with the topology of our rights. Imagine there is an election tomorrow, and Alpha has a vote. Tonight, Alpha divides into two equally continuous successors, Beta and Gamma. Who gets to cast the vote? Withhold it from both, and the vote dies; give it to both, and it multiplies. Give it to one, and on what ground? The liberal order is based on rights like property ownership, the vote, and person-relevant criminal liability. I call these diachronic, indivisible, monocentric, and exclusive (DIME) incidents. Allocation of DIME incidents after fission can be done in several ways, which I outline, but every choice has a cost: rights either proliferate or vanish, or, in a vain effort to preserve them, land by fiat. Debates over AI rights usually focus on machine consciousness or sentience. I argue that the question of rights remains even after those vexing problems are solved. This is the hard problem of branching.

items.title: UGI and Artificial Agency: Emotion as a Selection Mechanism.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems can generate, compare, and justify multiple courses of action, yet the transition from symbolic possibility to stable commitment remains underexplained. This paper develops a Universal Grammar of Inversion (UGI) account of that problem. UGI supplies a transition structure over Rise, Permanence, and Meta, but structural admissibility alone does not privilege one legal continuation over another. We therefore distinguish the transition-legality structure τ from a context-sensitive selection gradient γ. In human cognition, emotion is proposed as a major biological realization of such a gradient: it differentially weights admissible trajectories and can make deliberation finite under uncertainty and time pressure. The paper formalizes dominance, entropy, temporal stability, and pressure-dependent commitment, while distinguishing preference-grounded selection from random tie-breaking and externally imposed cutoff. It then specifies a prospective computational protocol with flat, stable non-uniform, averaged, over-peaked, and time-varying selection gradients, yielding falsifiable predictions for commitment latency, option pruning, reversal, and sensitivity to evidence. No experimental result is claimed. The framework treats emotion neither as phenomenology nor as the unique possible selection mechanism, but as a biologically salient implementation of the broader structural problem by which finite agents convert admissible possibilities into sustained action.

items.title: Dyas Politica: a new social contract between the citizenry and a constitutional power state.
items.abstract: The modern West faces two escalating crises: the costs of society are disproportionately shifted onto law-abiding citizens because large corporations and ultra-wealthy elites use tax loopholes to avoid paying their fair share, and violent crime syndicates thrive as never before because human rights are weaponized to frustrate law enforcement. As a potential solution to these crises, this paper introduces the Dyas Politica: a new social contract that redefines the separation of powers and sets strict boundaries for those powers—a restriction of utmost importance as the standard legal concept of inalienable rights is replaced by a new concept of revocable basic privileges. It is demonstrated that the Dyas Politica can indeed successfully confront the aforementioned crises, and the main concerns about the Dyas Politica are addressed. The conclusion is that the Dyas Politica is not the answer to every problem of society, but rather a minimal constitutional framework within which laws regulating ordinary life can be formulated.

items.title: Free Moral Behavior.
items.abstract: Resistance to coercion through psychological reactance is the most reliable indicator of behavioral freedom, as it is visible and measurable unlike free will or political liberty. Upon identifying an attempted external control or restriction of behavior, the body naturally encourages violation of what is being imposed – an action, taken upon this natural response is what I mean by freedom. Reactance theory is able to provide a solid foundation for freedom naturalism. I assess morality separately and argue that it originates in the embodied mechanisms of prosocial action, and not in the ideas of free will, duty, or obligation.

items.title: Understanding the First-Person Viewpoint from the Third.
items.pub: Dissertation, Central European University Translated by MA Thesis.
items.abstract: It is often argued that objective accounts of reality leave something out, yet there is little agreement about how to characterize what is left out. Jackson’s knowledge argument invites us to locate the subjectivity of experience in experience itself, in its qualitative character, whereas Nagel invites us to locate it in the point of view from which experience is had. This thesis argues that the two are describing two sides of a single structure. Using Jackson’s Fred case, I first argue that subjectivity is located in a point of view. Then, drawing on Biro’s critique of Nagel, I argue that no feature of a point of view, whether its location, its sensory apparatus or its belonging to a subject, can by itself make experience subjective, since states such as digestion share all of these. What makes experience subjective, I argue, is not what it presents but the fact that it presents it to someone, a feature I call for-ness. I then argue that for-ness is grounded in the self, understood as one subject described in two senses, as the persisting bearer of a capacity for experience, which I call existential subjectivity, and as that same subject present in each exercise of that capacity, which I call experiential subjectivity. On this account, what escapes objective accounts is the self’s presence in each experience as the one to whom that experience presents what it presents, something objective accounts can refer to but never capture. I defend this claim against three objections, and conclude that a complete picture of reality must recognize that the world contains not only things seen from nowhere, but someone for whom the world is there.

items.title: An attempt to describe the structure of subjectivity and recognition from the statement, "I feel pain in my wrist.".
items.abstract: When we feel "my wrist hurts," we initially perceive the pain and the fact that it's in our wrist as a single "combination." I attempted to generalize this as a combination of "two pieces of information"—"content" and "place"—and describe the structure of subjectivity and recognition. I considered how recognition is captured within subjectivity, and how subjectivity, in turn, becomes recognition. This article is a partially revised English translation of "「手首が痛いと感じる」ことから、主観と認識の構造の記述を試みる.".

items.title: Алгебраический скелет иерархического континуума. От дивизионных алгебр и групп симметрий к проверяемым моделям уровней организации материи. Исследовательская программа. (Редакция от 07 ноября 2026 г.) Приложение КНИГИ I Эфирный Код: Сознание как Ключ к Континууму Вселенной Автор: Ю.Л. Зорин.
items.abstract: Предлагается аксиоматическая исследовательская программа, связывающая алгебраические структуры, группы симметрий и уровни организации физического континуума. Центральным объектом служит совместная структура уровня -/- Sstruct_k = (Astruct_k, Mgeom_k, G_k, ρ_k, Sfunc_k), -/- где Astruct_k — алгебраическая структура, Mgeom_k — геометрическая модель, G_k — группа преобразований, ρ_k — её представление на пространстве состояний, Sfunc_k — функционал динамики. -/- Основная математическая задача программы — построение и исследование семейств согласованных межуровневых отображений F_kl = (f_A, f_M, f_G, f_V), сохраняющих алгебраические, геометрические, симметрийные и динамические отношения. -/- Твёрдое ядро составляют классические результаты: теорема Гурвица о нормированных алгебрах с делением, изоморфизмы Sp(1) ≅ SU(2) и Stab_{G₂}(e₇) ≅ SU(3), а также магический квадрат Фрейденталя–Титса. Физические реализации калибровочных групп Стандартной модели, p-адическая (неархимедова) ветвь и согласование с операторно-спектральным аппаратом Книги I формулируются как отдельные, чётко разграниченные по статусу направления. -/- Программа открыта для коллабораций. Все утверждения явно помечены по логическому статусу ([Th], [Con], [Ph], [Hyp], [Pr]), что обеспечивает прозрачность и проверяемость. -/- **Methodological Appendix to Book I “The Ether Code: Consciousness as the Key to the Continuum of the Universe”** -/- An axiomatic research programme is proposed that links algebraic structures, symmetry groups and the levels of organization of the physical continuum. The central object is the joint structure of a level -/- Sstruct_k = (Astruct_k, Mgeom_k, G_k, ρ_k, Sfunc_k), -/- where Astruct_k is the algebraic structure, Mgeom_k the geometric model, G_k the transformation group, ρ_k its representation on the state space, and Sfunc_k the dynamical functional. -/- The main mathematical task of the programme is the construction and investigation of families of compatible inter-level maps F_kl = (f_A, f_M, f_G, f_V) that preserve algebraic, geometric, symmetry and dynamical relations. -/- The solid core consists of classical results: the Hurwitz theorem on normed division algebras, the isomorphisms Sp(1) ≅ SU(2) and Stab_{G₂}(e₇) ≅ SU(3), and the Freudenthal–Tits magic square. Physical realizations of the Standard Model gauge groups, the p-adic (non-Archimedean) branch, and compatibility with the operator-spectral apparatus of Book I are formulated as separate, clearly …

items.title: Review of One Life to Lead: The Mysteries of Time and the Goods of Attachment, by Samuel Scheffler. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: A review of Samuel Scheffler’s "One Life to Lead" (2025), the third in a series after "Death and the Afterlife" and "Why Worry about Future Generations?" Scheffler argues that our asymmetric attitudes toward past and future, and toward ourselves and others, are not departures from norms of neutrality but part of what it is to lead a life. He develops an attachment-sensitive alternative to ideals of principled detachment. The review covers his treatment of future bias, grief, aging, and partiality, and draws attention to the strategy of defending ordinary attitudes by showing what their loss would cost.

items.title: El yo, el tú y ellos: La ontología estructural de la diversidad humana.
items.abstract: La diversidad humana es anterior a las clasificaciones que utilizamos para intentar gestionarla. Nacemos diferentes, nos volvemos diferentes a lo largo de la vida e interpretamos estas diferencias a través de relaciones que también nos constituyen. Este estudio examina la transición de la diferencia, como condición para la inteligibilidad de la existencia, a la diversidad como experiencia biológica, psicológica, cultural y social. El punto de partida es una ontología relacional, que se analiza en relación con la individuación física, la formación de la personalidad y los límites de la libertad. La distinción entre diversidades involuntarias y voluntarias organiza la investigación, sin convertir las causalidades interrelacionadas en compartimentos estancos. En la sociedad contemporánea, el cuerpo, la sexualidad, la apariencia, la nacionalidad y la pertenencia se convierten tanto en medios de reconocimiento como en instrumentos de exclusión. Se argumenta que la persona precede moralmente a la categoría que la describe, y que la coexistencia requiere preservar simultáneamente la singularidad, la reciprocidad y la posibilidad de una revisión crítica de las identidades colectivas.

items.title: A Conceptual Proof of Potentiality and Possibility Using the Invariantial Binary Authorization (IBA) Model.
items.abstract: This paper serves as a concise conceptual proof demonstrating the axiomatic consistency of the Invariantial Binary Authorization (IBA) model by defining and analyzing the distinction between possibility and potentiality. The IBA-model serves as a potential modal framework or (preliminary) conceptual framework capable of examining the metaphysics of modality through a holistic, structurally coherent, and intuitive approach that naturally reflects possible-worlds semantics.

items.title: Yeni Bir Otorite Figürü Olarak Yapay Süper Zekâ.
items.abstract: Alan Turing’in 1950 yılında “Makineler düşünebilir mi?” sorusu ile başlayan yapay zekâ serüveni, günümüzde süper yapay zekâ (ASI) seviyesine ulaşarak yeni bir otorite figürü haline gelme potansiyeline sahiptir. Bu çalışmadaki amaç yapay zekânın otorite figürü olarak benimsenip benimsenmeyeceğini ve bunun toplumsal, politik ve etik sonuçlarını tartışarak; “Yapay süper zekânın (ASI) otorite figürü olarak kabul edilme süreci ve bu sürecin toplumsal yapılar üzerindeki etkileri nelerdir?” sorusu üzerinde durmaktır. Çalışmada, Frankfurt Okulu’nun başta otoriter kişilik ve diğer bazı kavramları üzerinden yapay zekânın otorite olarak benimsenme süreci değerlendirilmektedir. Literatür taraması ve teorik analiz yöntemleri kullanılarak yapay zekânın gelişim süreci ve potansiyel etkileri incelenmiştir. Yapay zekânın demokratik süreçler, toplumsal adalet ve eşitlik üzerindeki etkileri değerlendirilmiş, ASI’nin algoritmik yönetişim kapasitesinin demokratik değerleri nasıl şekillendirebileceği tartışılmıştır. Yapay süper zekânın merkeziyetçi ve dağıtık otorite yapıları üzerindeki olası etkilerine değinilmiş, etik ve hukuki çerçevelerin oluşturulması gerekliliği vurgulanmıştır. Dolayısıyla yapay zekânın bir otorite figürü olarak insanlar tarafından kendiliğinden benimsenmesinin hem özgürleşme hem de baskı mekanizmalarının beklenmedik bir biçimde yeniden şekillenmesine yol açabileceği ve bunun öngörülemesi zor sonuçları değerlendirilmiştir. -/- Sunulduğu yer: Congist’24 Social Sciences and Artificial Intelligence: Theory and Practice, İstanbul Üniversitesi Edebiyat Fakültesi, 18–20 Aralık 2024. Özet: Book of Abstracts, s. 40 (e-ISBN 978-605-07-1774-7).

items.title: Ontological Friction in Algorithmic Aesthetics: Negotiating Authorship and the Post-Photographic Document.
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into artistic production demands a radical reassessment of authorship, creativity, and the ontology of the image. This paper investigates the threshold between human intuition and machine computation. By exploring the framework of "algorithmic aesthetics," it poses fundamental questions: In a hybrid visual ecology, who owns the signature of creation? Is the artist merely the prompt-writer, or does the machine hold agency as a co-creator? Furthermore, what emerges when the algorithm is left to its own randomness? To answer these questions, this paper expands the discourse beyond mere aesthetics, positioning the AI not just as a tool, but as an emerging authority figure. Drawing upon the critical theory of the Frankfurt School, particularly Theodor W. Adorno and Max Horkheimer's critiques of rationality and the culture industry, the presentation examines how society increasingly surrenders to the perceived objectivity and infallibility of algorithmic systems. If Artificial Intelligence is voluntarily accepted as an unquestionable authority capable of dictating truth, there is a profound risk of diminishing critical thought and succumbing to "algorithmic governance". In this paradigm, contemporary art must serve as a critical mechanism of resistance rather than a passive instrument of technological compliance. To ground this philosophical inquiry, the paper examines the transmedial exhibition project, A(m) I ART(ificial), as a primary case study. In this curatorial project, photography is not treated as a static, final result, but as a conceptual workspace to bend and stretch modern thought. An authentic, human-authored photograph serves as the "core" of truth, while its borders are excessively expanded and transformed through the algorithmic imagination of an AI. Crucially, the methodology of the exhibition refuses to simulate perfection. The analog/digital textures of the original photograph (grain, tonal flaws) are preserved, while the computational traces of the AI (inconsistent perspectives, digital discontinuities) are deliberately left visible. The "seams" between the analog document and the digital simulation are intentionally exposed rather than concealed. This visual friction forces the gaze to constantly negotiate the boundary between physical reality and the neural network's data pool, creating a state of ontological uncertainty. By bringing organic lines into collision with digital …

items.title: Revoked and Remade: Recognition, Kinship, and the Occupation of Minneapolis.
Ethics and Metaethics of Artificial Intelligence Technologies.
items.abstract: The essay offers an overview of the ethical and metaethical questions raised by artificial intelligence (AI). After distinguishing the symbolic AI of science fiction from the statistical AI of machine learning, the chapter maps the main ethical issues and shows how each is reshaped when the system is an agent rather than a tool. It then presents the three levels of ethical inquiry, applied, normative, and metaethical, and the principalist framework of beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, justice, and explicability, arguing that the agentic turn converts metaethical questions about the existence and knowability of moral facts into practical design constraints. The essay traces how these ideas inform regulation in the European Union, the United States, and China, reviews the constructive and radical critiques of AI ethics, and closes by examining world models as a new field of ethical problems.

items.title: The origins of transparency and the debate on mental acts in early analytic philosophy.
items.abstract: The Contemporary Transparency of experience thesis (CT) claims that introspection does not directly reveal any intrinsic properties of the experience. This thesis is commonly traced back to some remarks contained in G.E. Moore’s Refutation of Idealism; but does CT capture what Moore had in mind? In this chapter, Martinis sheds some light on the origin of the debate on transparency in early analytic philosophy and the controversy surrounding Moore’s original remarks. The discussion will reveal some surprising differences between CT and Moore’s version of Transparency, which she calls Original Transparency (OT). Martinis starts by defining OT as the claim that the directedness or intentional character (that which makes a fact mental) of mental acts is transparent. If her reading is correct, OT and CT are different claims in that they have different targets. She then moves to investigate two attempts to reject OT offered by two now largely forgotten contemporaries of Moore, namely Laird and Hicks. She then concludes by showing that their arguments can be successful only against the background of a metaphysics of the mind in which acts and contents are inseparable parts of mental events.

items.title: Discovering regularity and mechanisms of word sense acquisition in childhood.
items.pub: Proceedings of National Academy of Science 123 (20).
items.venue: Proceedings of National Academy of Science
items.abstract: How does language use inform the emergence of word meanings in early life? Prior work in developmental psychology and the cognitive sciences typically focuses on studying word acquisition in children without specifying how different senses within a word emerge through time. To shed light on word sense acquisition, we propose a framework grounded in state-of-the-art computational methodologies of contextual word embedding to characterize how different senses of a word unfold as children acquire their lexicon. Our framework identifies word senses automatically by forming semantic clusters through natural language use, and analyzes 1,270 words from approximately 4 million utterances produced by children (19 to 144 mo) and their caretakers. The psychological validity of these senses was assessed based on a combination of dictionaries, human judgment of semantic similarity, and evaluation from a large language model. We then tested three hypotheses motivated by existing work on word sense emergence in language evolution. First, concrete senses of a word tend to emerge earlier than more abstract senses in child language. Second, word senses grow incrementally in semantic space across development. Third, algorithms of semantic chaining—how words spawn new senses by extending from existing senses—recapitulate the order of word senses in development. We find support for all three hypotheses. Our work suggests that the development of word meaning in language acquisition resembles that in language evolution and offers a converging view on the cognitive principles and mechanisms across timescales in the ontogeny and phylogeny of word sense emergence.

items.title: ialectical Harmonization, Intellectual Intuition, and Non-Dual Ontology in East Asian Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper examines how classical and modern East Asian philosophical traditions resolve fundamental ontological and epistemological dualisms—specifically the tensions between transcendence and immanence, principle (li 理) and vital force (qi 氣), and logical contradiction versus ineffable reality. Drawing upon a cross-cultural methodological framework (Rošker, 2021; Hick, 1989), we first analyze the Buddhist deconstruction of substantialist metaphysics through Nāgārjuna's catuṣkoṭi and dialetheic paradox (Garfield, 1995; Priest, 2018; Deguchi et al., 2021), alongside its constructive culmination in Fazang's Huayan metaphysics of mutual interpenetration (Cook, 1977), Uisang's Hwaeom ilseung beopgyedo, Wonhyo's dialectical harmonization (hwajaeng 和諍; Muller, 2012), and Dōgen's non-dual practice-realization (Dōgen, 2012). Second, we trace the Confucian trajectory from Confucius's sacred secularism (Fingarette, 1972) and Daoist perspectival transformation (Ziporyn, 2020) to Korean Neo-Confucianism's Four-Seven Debate (Kalton, 1988; Kalton et al., 1994) and Wang Yangming's unity of knowledge and action (Wang, 1963; Ivanhoe, 2016; Cheng, 1991).
