Second, a mother who conceived through her own free act owes the child her continued bodily support, even when precautions failed (C2, T5). Whoever is the author of another’s dependence answers for it, just as a careful driver who strikes a pedestrian must still stop and help. The duty extends to the dependence so authored, and no further. Third, where the pregnancy threatens the mother’s life, or would permanently close her field of freedom, intervention to protect her is permitted (T6, T6*). The rule never demands two deaths where one can be prevented, and it never permits sacrificing one who would otherwise survive. Fourth, after rape the child’s standing is undiminished, and killing remains forbidden (T7). But the duty of continued bodily support rests on authorship, and a woman who authored nothing is not bound by it. The costs of the wrong belong to the aggressor and to the community, never to the child. Fifth, the gravity of the act is not the guilt of the woman (T9). Very often the real murderer at the door stands outside her: the partner who abandons, the family that coerces, the employer, poverty, the state. Those who press on the door share the debt, and the woman is owed a path of restoration, not a sentence. Sixth, the state may protect the unborn, but it may never occupy the mother (T11, C3). China’s coerced abortions and Romania’s coerced births fail the same test. A law that forbids abortion while leaving the mother to carry the burden alone loses its legitimacy, even …

items.title: Toward an Epistemology of Open Systems.
items.abstract: The Gödel incompleteness theorems are often read as marking an impassable horizon for formal reason: every consistent, recursively axiomatized system capable of expressing arithmetic contains unprovable truths and cannot prove its own consistency [1]. This article proposes a different reading, in dialogue with a philosophical study devoted to an open problem in theoretical computer science [2]. We formulate three articulated metatheoretical principles. The first, the principle of dynamic coherence: within a hierarchy of conceptual frameworks, one and the same statement can take different truth values at different levels without inducing global incoherence, provided that each extension of the structure preserves a form of internal coherence; local divergence then signals depth and expansion, not instability. The second, the principle of reflective memory: in an open learning system, active memory, understood as the preservation, transformation, and reintegration of the traces of prior states, is the necessary condition for the emergence of second-order knowledge; memory is therefore not a mere archive but the operator of transcendence. The third notion, numerical verticality: a cognitive system of fixed internal dimension can enrich, refine, and reorganize its representations without bound, but cannot change the representational framework itself; such a framework change requires the intervention of a meta-system. We articulate these principles with established results: the relativity of satisfaction across models of set theory, the topological invariance of dimension, the neurobiology of memory reconsolidation and of complementary learning systems, and the geometry of neural manifolds. We conclude that open systems should be conceived not as incoherent machines but as stratified architectures whose coherence is of a higher order.

items.title: Book of Abstracts: 4th Annual Online Conference of the International Society for the Philosophy of the Sciences of the Mind.
items.pub: International Society for the Philosophy of the Sciences of the Mind.
items.venue: International Society for the Philosophy of the Sciences of the Mind
items.abstract: Embodied Insights: Interoception in Psychedelic Epistemology -/- Psychedelic epistemology is currently deadlocked on several fronts. Claims that metaphysical reality is revealed by psychedelic experience produce mutually irreconcilable conclusions. Work on psychological insights under psychedelics has connected those experiences to therapeutic benefits (Kugel et al. 2025), but methods of epistemic verification remain unclear. Meanwhile, some epistemologists have questioned whether psychedelic experience itself can lead to the acquisition of knowledge, or perhaps just increase understanding (Fink 2022). Psychedelic insights involving bodily states, addiction, and health may provide ideal test cases because such claims can be triangulated across multiple forms of evidence, such as physiological measures, validated self-report instruments, and behavioural outcomes. This presentation proposes that interoception—the brain’s sensing and interpretation of the organism’s internal states and homeostatic needs—is an underexamined epistemic source with major implications for psychedelic epistemology. I argue that interoceptive epistemic performance cannot be reduced to the veridical detection of bodily signals (Garfinkel et al. 2015). Sensory systems track properties relative to organismic interests, while embodied appraisals represent what bodily changes mean for an organism’s concerns and well-being (Prinz 2004). Such appraisals can succeed or fail. Danger may be detected or overlooked, benign arousal misrepresented as threat, and damaging states assigned insufficient salience. Interoception therefore operates at an epistemically significant interface between bodily sensation and cognitive appraisal, where physiological information contributes to representations with conditions of correctness. On this account, interoception enables and constrains knowledge not only through detection, but through appraisal and salience (Seth 2013). Epistemic improvement occurs when altered appraisal more accurately represents the significance of bodily states for the organism’s health, needs, and goals. 165 Although psychedelic experiences are highly variable, insights related to substance use, diet, and exercise show recurring tendencies toward health-promoting orientations and behavioural changes across clinical and naturalistic contexts (Teixeira et al. 2022). These convergent patterns call for epistemic explanation. I argue that psychedelic alterations to the salience and …

items.title: Something is rotten in the state of knowledge: the epistemic costs of automating search.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming the default way many people search for information. We argue that this shift carries epistemic costs that are easy to overlook. Treating search broadly as information foraging, we distinguish manual search, in which the searcher directs the exploration and does the work of evaluating and connecting what they find, from automated search, in which that work is handed to an AI system. We advance two sets of arguments. The first concerns epistemic capacity: manual search builds a deeper, more resilient understanding of particular questions and stronger priors for searching well. The second concerns epistemic diversity: manual search exposes individuals to unexpected ideas and leads populations of searchers to more varied conclusions. Automated search erodes both, and its convenience combined with the sycophantic nature of LLMs makes the losses easy to accept and hard to see. Across society, we expect a new form of epistemic inequality between those who still do the work of search and those who do not, and perhaps less obviously a narrowing of society’s collective open-endedness. We conclude that human hands should stay deeply involved in the work of exploration and judgment. Since few users currently ask their models to challenge them systematically, and companies have little incentive to change the default, this will require a cultural response that makes the costs of automated search visible.

items.title: The Glial-Orchestrated Cognition (GOC) Model with Cellular Consciousness: A Biological Framework for Consciousness, Information, and Cognition.
items.abstract: Current neuroscience typically assumes that consciousness, information processing, and cognition arise from neuronal activity. This neuron-centric view cannot explain why consciousness persists when cognition shuts down, why cognition can operate unconsciously, or why glial cells, which outnumber neurons, are essential for coherent thought. This paper introduces the Glial-Orchestrated Cognition (GOC) model, which separates three domains: (1) consciousness as an intrinsic property of all living cells, (2) information as a specialized function of neurons, and (3) cognition as the unified informational state produced by glial coordination. In this framework, human conscious experience is a composite phenomenon: cellular consciousness combined with glial-integrated cognition. In one line: the cell is the source of consciousness; glia are the synchronizer. The synchronizing mechanism is formalized here as choir coherence (§[sec:choir]), defined canonically for the family’s communications manuscripts. The model provides a biologically grounded, experimentally testable architecture for understanding the mind and the unity of experience.

items.title: 自分という認識の成立過程の検討.
items.abstract: 私は、自分を「その人にとっての『私』のこと」、「その人自身のこと」であると考えます。では、自分という認識はどのようにして成立するのでしょうか。私は以前の考察から得た４つの前提条件と照らし合わせながら、自分という認識の成立過程を考察しました。.

items.title: DKDA - Duale Kodier- und Dekodierarchitektur.
items.abstract: Zusammenfassung Die Duale Kodier- und Dekodierarchitektur (DKDA) schlägt einen zusammenhängenden Mechanismus menschlicher Kommunikation vor. Dual bezeichnet die Senderseite der Kodierung und die Empfängerseite der Dekodierung. Auf der Sendeseite unterscheidet DKDA Bauen und Verpacken; auf der Empfängerseite greift sie Nachbauen und Entpacken auf. Aus ihrer Kreuzung ergeben sich vier mögliche Kombinationen. Der Schwerpunkt dieses Konzepts ist die senderseitige Spiegelung: Ausformulierung oder Verdichtung hängen von einem vermuteten Empfängermodell ab und verteilen Rekonstruktionsarbeit und Passungsrisiko unterschiedlich. Eine latente Dekodierdiskrepanz (LDD) bezeichnet eine registrierte Inkonsistenz, die den laufenden Rekonstruktionspfad noch nicht wirksam unterbricht. Kosten und Folgen einer Klärung oder Fortsetzung hängen von Situation, Ziel und aktivierbarer Vorverdichtung ab. Das Konzept befindet sich in laufender Ausarbeitung und ist nicht empirisch validiert.

items.title: Inverse Reconstruction and Endogenous Generation of Interpretive Revision: Recovering R under Fixed Quantum Evidence.
items.abstract: Whole Pattern, Local Event (WPLE) gives ontological priority to the Whole while preserving established quantum predictions and the reality of localized physical events. This paper formalizes two related problems concerning interpretive revision under fixed quantum evidence. In inverse reconstruction, a destination C and evidence A are specified and a constrained revision R is reconstructed in the motivating relation A + R = C. In endogenous generation, the initial evidence and interpretive framework are examined without specifying C; candidate revisions arise from independently testable inconsistencies, failures of claimed deductive license, and declared standards of explanatory adequacy. Both procedures use a protected empirical package, an explicitly revisable belief base, independently specified hypothesis and ontology-comparison spaces, and inspectable appraisal standards. A finite propositional reconstruction exhibits multiple inverse solutions and a separate target-free calculation in which conflict sets yield a revision before any destination is chosen. Quantum applications address localized detector records, two-path interference, and GHZ global correlations. The calculations preserve states, observables, instruments, and Born-rule predictions while testing the inferences assigned to them. An analysis of context-conditioned computation clarifies how external information can redirect explanatory priorities and how analogous audits can generate candidate revisions internally, without equating transformer attention with quantum dynamics. The result is a methodological specification of how interpretive correction can be reconstructed or generated. Whole-priority remains WPLE's affirmative abductive ontological proposal, subject to independent explanatory appraisal. WPLE Framework Anchors: This paper is part of the Whole Pattern, Local Event (WPLE) framework series.

items.title: Testing the Core Emotion Framework: A Proposed Protocol for a Randomised Study of Emotional Cycling and of Practitioner Prediction of Dominant Powers.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) describes ten inner powers that everyone has, grouped in three centres (Head, Heart and Gut), and holds that distress comes from emotional rigidity, in which a few powers fuse and suppress the others. Its advanced practice, Emotional Cycling, is said to free the powers, restore their independence and increase emotional flexibility. Existing data fit several of the framework’s stated claims about rigidity and release, but no dataset records anyone doing the practice, so its central claim has not been tested. This article sets out a proposed protocol for testing it. Study A is a three-arm randomised trial comparing four weeks of daily Emotional Cycling with a matched neutral-movement practice and with daily journaling; the primary outcome is a person’s rated ability to ignite and release each power. Study B is a separate, exploratory test of whether a trained CEF practitioner, after a brief standardised observation and with predictions sealed and timestamped in advance, can identify a person’s dominant and weak powers better than chance, judged by a permutation test. Hypotheses, measures, sample-size assumptions and criteria for “supported”, “not supported” and “inconclusive” are fixed in advance. The protocol has not been run and is not a preregistration; it will be registered before any data are collected. Researchers, laboratories and trained CEF practitioners are invited to run or co-run the study, in full or as a pilot.

items.title: Why You Should Be Miserable.
items.abstract: There is a deeply plausible and popularly held value theoretic principle that the good merits love and the bad merits hate. This principle holds that it is intrinsically good to take a pro-attitude, such as being pleased by or enjoying, toward objects or states of affairs that are themselves intrinsically good, and it is intrinsically good to take a con-attitude, such as being pained by toward objects or states of affairs that are intrinsically bad. From this principle and four plausible asymmetries about value, one can formulate a coherent argument to the conclusion that you should be miserable. While one might take this conclusion as a reductio against the principle that the good merits love and the bad merits hate, it is argued that the principle stands nonetheless.

items.title: Akratic thinking.
items.abstract: Akratic action is voluntarily acting against one’s better judgment. Akratic belief is believing against one’s better judgment. We here provide an account of a phenomenon that sits somewhere between the two: “akratic thinking.” This is where we engage in a thought process against our better judgment. While the idea of akratic thinking has been tentatively considered before, no account has yet been offered of it. This is what we’ll offer here. Our account will seek to show how akratic thinking is possible, the different forms it can take, and the kind of irrationality involved. We’ll also explore how the notion of akratic thinking can provide an alternative explanation for some ostensible cases of akratic belief, and the implications it may have for our understanding of certain mental disorders.

items.title: The role of values in curiosity: cognitive and epistemic issues.
items.abstract: This paper examines the role of values in the emergence of curiosity, focusing on its so-called “chicken-egg problem”: do we become curious because we already care about something, or do we start caring because we are curious about it? Drawing on an embodied and ecological perspective on cognition, as well as insights from Ignorance Studies, I analyze the affective and epistemic conditions under which curiosity arises. I defend two main claims: (1) curiosity emerges as an embodied response to the affordances of unfamiliar objects, which agents engage with because they already value them in some way; and (2) once curiosity arises, it reshapes how agents care for that content. To capture this dynamic, I propose a compound definition of curiosity as a bodily, emotional, and cognitive state, where caring guides curiosity and curiosity reveals caring.

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung; Teil 5.
items.abstract: Mit dem fünften Teil richtet sich die Untersuchung auf eine Frage, die für das Leben und Handeln des Individuums von grundlegender Bedeutung ist: Wie verwendet der Mensch das, was er durch seine bisherigen Erfahrungen und Überlegungen verstanden hat, um sich unter neuen Bedingungen zurechtzufinden? Die vorausgehenden vier Teile haben erklärt, wie das Individuum aus seinen Erfahrungen bestimmte Einheiten und Zusammenhänge bildet, diese wiedererkennt und Veränderungen versteht. Außerdem wurde untersucht, wie es solche Veränderungen mithilfe von Begriffen erklären kann. Damit ist jedoch noch nicht geklärt, welche Bedeutung dieses Verständnis für seine weitere Orientierung besitzt. Denn es ist ein Unterschied, ob jemand eine Veränderung erkennt und erklären kann oder ob er aus diesem Verständnis Erwartungen entwickelt, Handlungsmöglichkeiten erkennt und entscheidet, wie er sich unter veränderten Bedingungen verhalten soll. Gerade dieser Übergang vom Verstehen bereits gebildeter Wirklichkeit zu ihrer Verwendung für weitere Erfahrungen und mögliche Handlungen bildet den Ausgangspunkt des fünften Teils. Damit das Individuum sich orientieren kann, muss es auf das zurückgreifen können, was es bereits erfahren und verstanden hat. Es muss beispielsweise Menschen, Gegenstände, Situationen und Beziehungen wiedererkennen können, um Erwartungen darüber zu entwickeln, was unter bestimmten Umständen geschehen könnte. Diese Wiedererkennbarkeit beruht auf der Stabilisierung zuvor gebildeter Einheiten. Doch nicht alles, was ein Individuum wiedererkennt oder versteht, ist für seine weitere Orientierung gleichermaßen bedeutsam. Welche Erfahrungen es beachtet, welche Erwartungen es entwickelt und welche Handlungsmöglichkeiten es in Betracht zieht, hängt auch davon ab, was für es unter den jeweiligen Bedingungen wichtig wird. Hier kommt der emotional fundierten Relevanzbildung eine entscheidende Bedeutung zu. Orientierung entsteht somit nicht allein dadurch, dass das Individuum über eine bereits geordnete Wirklichkeit verfügt, sondern dadurch, dass es diese Ordnung entsprechend seinen jeweiligen Erfahrungen, Bedürfnissen und Erwartungen für sein weiteres Verstehen und Handeln verwendet. Dabei kann es sich nicht darauf verlassen, dass bisherige Erfahrungen immer bestätigt werden. Eine vertraute Situation kann sich anders entwickeln als erwartet, eine bisher erfolgreiche Handlung kann ihre Wirkung verfehlen und eine bislang verlässliche Beziehung kann sich verändern. Orientierung …

items.title: Change from the Perspektive of the Unity Formation; Part V.
items.abstract: With the fifth part, the investigation turns to a question of fundamental importance for the life and actions of the individual: How does the individual use what they have understood through previous experiences and reflections to find their way under new conditions? The preceding four parts have explained how the individual forms determinate unities and relations from experience, recognizes them again, and understands changes. They have also examined how the individual can explain such changes by means of concepts. However, it has not yet been clarified what significance this understanding has for the individual's further orientation. For there is a difference between recognizing and explaining a change and using this understanding to develop expectations, identify possibilities of action, and decide how to behave under changed conditions. It is precisely this transition from understanding an already formed actuality to using it for further experiences and possible actions that constitutes the starting point of the fifth part. In order to orient themselves, individuals must be able to draw upon what they have already experienced and understood. For example, they must be able to recognize people, objects, situations, and relations in order to develop expectations about what might happen under certain circumstances. This recognizability rests upon the stabilization of previously formed unities. Yet not everything that an individual recognizes or understands is equally significant for their further orientation. Which experiences they attend to, which expectations they develop, and which possibilities of action they consider also depend on what becomes important to them under the respective conditions. Here, emotionally grounded relevance formation is of decisive importance. Orientation therefore arises not merely because the individual possesses an already ordered actuality, but because they use this order for further understanding and action in accordance with their respective experiences, needs, and expectations. In doing so, they cannot assume that previous experiences will always be confirmed. A familiar situation may develop differently than expected, a previously successful action may fail to produce its intended effect, and a relationship that has so far proved reliable may change. Orientation must therefore not only draw upon already formed and stabilized relations but also allow for their examination and modification. On this basis, it becomes …

items.title: AI, Epistemic Relations, and Testimonial Outsourcing.
items.abstract: Generative AI “companions” are increasingly integrated into higher education as always-available interlocutors that offer feedback, explanation, and encouragement. This article examines how such systems reshape the epistemic relations through which students speak, are heard, and come to count as knowers, and argues that companion-style AIs can disrespect epistemic relations in systematic ways. Students may become less able, and less willing, to testify on their own in genuinely reciprocal spaces (such as class discussions, office hours, and peer groups), habitually relying on their AI companions instead. Call this phenomenon testimonial outsourcing: a structural tendency to outsource one’s testimonial activity, which functions as a self-imposed, technologically mediated analogue of gaslighting. Students come to treat the AI’s outputs as more reliable than their own judgment and expressive capacities, thereby eroding their epistemic self-trust and cultivating a distorted conception of legitimate epistemic expectations. This article concludes by drawing implications for AI design and educational policy, placing constraints that preserve “non-mediated” spaces of speech, require explicit AI transparency, and build frictions that redirect students back toward interpersonal relations.

items.title: Poseidon’s Rotors: An Analogy for Koopman Theory.
items.abstract: This document develops an analogy for Koopman theory. It straddles the line between analogy and example. It is meant to provide intuition regarding the theory and to illustrate its unintuitive power; it is not exhaustive of its nuances. In particular, the analogy focuses on decaying and steady modes only; growing modes, which arise in unstable dynamics, are omitted.

items.title: Level separation: From ethics to epistemology.
items.abstract: Ethical consequentialists often apply a strict level separation between the normative status of practical inquiries and the normative status of the intentions they produce. This paper has two aims. The first is to formulate and defend a generalized version of level separation that expands its ambitions from ethics into epistemology. The second is to use this generalized account of level separation to shed light on both traditional and recent questions within epistemology. The result is an expanded account of level separation and novel test cases for the account against traditional and emerging questions in epistemology.

items.title: Anatomía y patología del poder: un estudio dialéctico.
items.abstract: Los seres humanos viven en una paradoja que sus extraordinarios avances técnicos no han resuelto: dependen de sistemas colectivos para seguir existiendo, pero esos mismos sistemas con frecuencia se convierten en instrumentos mediante los cuales una minoría somete la vida de la mayoría a fines que esta no eligió ni autorizó realmente. Este libro explora esa paradoja al distinguir la producción social de capacidades compartidas de su apropiación por parte de individuos, grupos e instituciones. La tesis inicial concibe el poder social como la capacidad organizada de una comunidad para orientar la conducta individual de modo que personas interdependientes sostengan un mundo común. La antítesis examina la perversión de esa relación, en la que los mecanismos de la vida comunitaria sirven a intereses particulares mientras trasladan costos y riesgos a otros. La síntesis desarrolla la noción de poder corregible: una autoridad organizada de modo que quienes están sujetos a decisiones de importancia conserven medios efectivos para comprenderlas, impugnarlas, modificarlas y, cuando sea necesario, sustituir a las autoridades responsables. El estudio combina la clarificación conceptual con la comparación evolutiva, la interpretación histórica, el análisis de la economía política y la evidencia conductual. Distingue las explicaciones evolutivas de las intenciones conscientes, la descripción histórica de la aprobación moral y el estudio psicológico de la dominación del diagnóstico clínico. Rechaza tratar la sociabilidad o la libertad personal como bienes absolutos que puedan prescindir el uno del otro. Una colectividad puede proteger la vida mientras persigue a sus miembros; un individuo puede resistir la opresión mientras busca otra forma de tiranía personal. La cuestión decisiva, por tanto, es cómo se organizan esas relaciones. El argumento concluye que un futuro defendible exige instituciones que distribuyan la capacidad de corregir las propias instituciones, aseguren las bases materiales de la capacidad de actuar, respeten la pluralidad humana y reconozcan las dependencias ecológicas que hacen posibles los proyectos políticos. Ese futuro no promete eliminar el conflicto. Ofrece la posibilidad de que el conflicto no tenga que reproducir perpetuamente la dominación.

items.title: Anatomie et pathologie du pouvoir : une étude dialectique.
items.abstract: Les êtres humains vivent dans un paradoxe que leurs extraordinaires avancées techniques n’ont pas résolu : ils dépendent de systèmes collectifs pour continuer d’exister, mais ces mêmes systèmes deviennent fréquemment des instruments par lesquels une minorité soumet la vie de la majorité à des fins que celle-ci n’a pas réellement choisies ni autorisées. Ce livre explore ce paradoxe en distinguant la production sociale de capacités partagées de leur appropriation par des individus, des groupes et des institutions. La thèse initiale conçoit le pouvoir social comme la capacité organisée d’une communauté à orienter la conduite individuelle de telle sorte que des personnes interdépendantes soutiennent un monde commun. L’antithèse examine la perversion de cette relation, où les mécanismes de la vie communautaire servent des intérêts particuliers tout en transférant les coûts et les risques à d’autres. La synthèse développe la notion de pouvoir corrigible : une autorité organisée de telle sorte que ceux qui sont soumis à des décisions importantes conservent des moyens effectifs de les comprendre, de les contester, de les modifier et, lorsque cela est nécessaire, de remplacer les autorités responsables. L’étude associe la clarification conceptuelle à la comparaison évolutive, à l’interprétation historique, à l’analyse de l’économie politique et à l’analyse des données comportementales. Elle distingue les explications évolutives des intentions conscientes, la description historique de l’approbation morale et l’étude psychologique de la domination du diagnostic clinique. Elle refuse de traiter la sociabilité ou la liberté personnelle comme des biens absolus qui pourraient se passer l’un de l’autre. Une collectivité peut protéger la vie tout en persécutant ses membres ; un individu peut résister à l’oppression tout en cherchant une autre forme de tyrannie personnelle. La question décisive est donc de savoir comment ces relations sont organisées. L’argument conclut qu’un avenir défendable exige des institutions qui distribuent la capacité de corriger les institutions elles-mêmes, assurent les bases matérielles de la capacité d’agir, respectent la pluralité humaine et reconnaissent les dépendances écologiques qui rendent possibles les projets politiques. Cet avenir ne promet pas d’éliminer le conflit. Il offre la possibilité que le conflit n’ait pas à reproduire perpétuellement la domination.

items.title: On the Possible Worlds Defined by Formal Ontologies: Rethinking the “One Ontology, One Possible World” Principle in the Context of Interoperable Systems.
items.abstract: The “one ontology, one possible world” principle holds that every formal ontology defines a single, determinate possible world, thereby leaving no room for misunderstanding in the communication of its content. Framed as an applied philosophy case study in ontology engineering and digital document interoperability, this paper argues that the principle is not universally valid. First, it shows that an isolated ontology—considered together with its entities, the formal language in which it is expressed, and the underlying assumptions governing the management of known and unknown information—can indeed determine a unique, determined world. Second, it examines a cross-format interaction between such an ontology and a document that is neither itself an ontology nor a mere replica of the ontology’s informational content, showing that this interaction disrupts logical closure and generates a plurality of possible worlds. The paper therefore concludes that the “one ontology, one possible world” principle is context-dependent rather than universal and calls for a more pragmatic, context-sensitive approach to ontology design and communication, particularly in interoperable environments.

items.title: Pascalian Resistance Without Moral Facts: A Moral Irrealist Response to Joshua Brecka.
items.abstract: Joshua Brecka argues that the punitive structure of traditional Pascalian wagers supplies a moral reason to wager against God and makes such resistance supererogatory: morally good but beyond duty. This paper asks what survives of that argument under a specified moral error theory. It does not establish error theory or attribute moral realism to Brecka merely because he uses moral language. Its conditional conclusion is that an error theorist cannot endorse the positive moral judgments needed to classify resistance as literally supererogatory. Expressivist and other non-realist interpretations require separate treatment. The paper also identifies problems independent of error theory: refusal of allegiance does not entail atheism, severe personal risk does not by itself establish moral optionality, and finite aversion to allegiance cannot simply outweigh an infinite payoff. Resistance may nevertheless be supported by an agent's informed commitments, and punitive theology may conflict with a believer's own understanding of divine love and justice. A final proposal considers a deist who regards any actual God as loving and supportive of evidence-responsive inquiry. Given further explicit assumptions, that deist has an additional reason to reject invitations to manufacture belief through rewards or threats. This is a conditional challenge to the invitation's justification, not evidence for atheism merely from disapproval.

items.title: Toward Nurturing Productive Clinician-AI Disagreement in Medicine.
items.abstract: We agree with Pozzi et al. (2026) regarding their assessment of three approaches for resolving disagreements between human clinicians and AI systems. Indeed, disagreements in medical decision-making, involving AI or not, are a feature of medical practice (rather than a bug), and those disagreements can be epistemically valuable. However, we aim to advance their argument by offering two recommendations for nurturing the conditions of possibility for productive clinician-AI disagreement in medicine, emerging from the premise that disagreement, while epistemically valuable, can reach resolution based on flawed reasoning or other epistemically irrelevant features. The first reason that disagreement may fail to be productive is related to material conditions that may affect the epistemic standing of the knowers involved (Zubčić 2022). A second reason is related to issues regarding the fair distribution of and access to epistemic credit and resources (Fricker 2007). Given the possibility of badly resolved disagreements, we hold that epistemically valuable disagreements in clinician-AI medicine, and disagreements in medicine more generally, depend on paying attention to addressing more foundational issues regarding material conditions and epistemic capital. -/- Shussett, D., & Dubljević, V. (2026). Toward Nurturing Productive Clinician-AI Disagreement in Medicine. The American Journal of Bioethics, 26(11), 129–132.

items.title: Shame and the Relational Self: A Philosophical Account.
INVERTED MIGRATION: A Synthecratic Model of Transborder Development, Integration, and Community Capacity Assessment.
items.abstract: This article proposes the concept of Inverted Migration, a model of transborder development in which people living outside their country or community of origin can contribute to its development without necessarily returning physically. The concept shifts the analytical focus from population movement itself to the organization of people’s voluntary participation in territorial development through knowledge, professional competencies, social networks, entrepreneurial initiatives, partnerships, and other forms of cooperation. Within the Synthecracy methodology, Inverted Migration is considered an adaptive process that combines the identification of social needs, data collection and verification, analysis, knowledge synthesis, scenario simulation, responsible decision-making, implementation, auditing, and social learning. Particular attention is paid to the conceptual architecture of the Inverted Migration Simulation Platform (IMSP), a digital platform proposed for development as a web-based tool for preliminary analysis of a community’s development opportunities. Community representatives would be able to enter data on population, needs, resources, infrastructure, potential participants, and constraints in order to obtain an analytical assessment of two principal scenarios: integrating participants into an existing community or establishing a new settlement. Simulation results are intended to show potential opportunities, resource gaps, risks, critical conditions, and questions requiring additional verification. The article formulates a definition of Inverted Migration, eight principles, spatial models, the conceptual architecture of a simulation tool, and hypotheses for further testing. The proposed model is conceptual in status and requires further theoretical comparison, prototype development, and empirical evaluation.

items.title: The Primate of All Creation as a Responsibility: A Conditional Analysis of Human Primacy through the Interpretability of Animal Communication.
items.abstract: Humanity has long described itself as the primate of all creation, a phrase that reads naturally as a claim of status. This paper asks what that claim entails once large language models (LLMs) make the analysis and mediation of animal communication a realistic research programme. -/- The familiar question about artificial intelligence is whether machines can think like humans. We reverse it: have humans genuinely tried to understand other forms of life? Taking nonhuman animals as the subject, we distinguish the classification of signals, their semantic interpretation, and reciprocal communication. -/- We introduce interpretability across species, the decoding and mediation of communication between living species so that its contents become mutually understandable, as a concept distinct from the translatability of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), a substrate-independent framework that separates operational structure from its representations. -/- We then examine a conditional thought experiment: if animal communication became interpretable and its contents qualitatively comparable to human culture, what would follow for humanity’s understanding of its own position? The claim of primacy could no longer rest on a presumption of incomprehension. We argue that it must be reread as a responsibility: to attempt to understand other life, and to respond to what is understood. -/- The paper derives no legal regime and no unconditional duty to comply with what other animals communicate, and it does not claim that cultural equivalence has been demonstrated. Published on November 2, 2026. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23898013.

items.title: Why First Philosophy Refuses to Die: Sexuality, Resistance, and the Recursive Return of Ground.
items.abstract: What if the oldest question in philosophy—"what is the ultimate ground of reality?"—cannot be answered, yet also cannot be abandoned? This paper traces an unconventional route from the analysis of sexual experience to a transformed conception of first philosophy. Beginning with the claim that sexuality involves not merely biological disposition but a three-dimensional interaction among the individual-organismic, the social-symbolic, and the material-objectual, we develop a relational account of experience as an event constituted through embodied, social, and material relations. Extending this structure to feeling, life-tendency, and resistance, we argue that resistance is not simply an obstacle to desire but a generative condition whose experiential valence depends on relational context. Modeled recursively as Rₙ → Gₙ → Rₙ₊₁, this pattern operates at both individual and social levels: meaning systems stabilize collective life until they collapse, prompting reorganization. Traditional first philosophy dies when its demand for an external, fixed foundation is placed inside the process it seeks to explain. Yet grounding itself persists. First philosophy returns—not as the search for a final foundation outside becoming, but as the inquiry into how reality recursively generates, stabilizes, contests, and revises grounds from within. The death and return of first philosophy thus become a reflexive demonstration of recursive ontology itself.

items.title: (Dis)continuity of Artificial Reason: On the Gap between Generality and Coherence_preprint.
items.abstract: Superintelligent AI agents (ASI) are typically ascribed two defining qualities: rational coherence, meaning their preferences satisfy decision-theoretic axioms that humans routinely violate, and general intelligence, meaning cross-domain capabilities that exceed human cognitive performance. However, these qualities are arguably in tension. Coherence is what is appealed to in order to understand how an ASI might differ from us, whereas generality is grasped through close comparison of the ASI to human intelligence. I argue that the complexity–coherence tradeoff can explain the crux of this tension. Studies of animal behaviour often show that less cognitively complex agents prove more rationally coherent than humans. Animals also seem less generally intelligent. This suggests a connection between the notions of complexity and generality. If cognitive complexity overlaps with general intelligence, then the complexity–coherence tradeoff is relevant to whether we ought to model ASI behaviour in terms of coherence. Available data suggests two classes of agents or cognitive processes: cognitively complex but incoherent or cognitively simple but coherent. The constitution of ASI fits neither category, creating a gap between what is currently known and supposed ASI. I argue that AI theorists ought to account for how ASI agents might cross this gap.

items.title: When Human Values Become Rewards: Ethical Frameworks and the Moral Translation Problem in AI Alignment.
items.abstract: Choosing a reward for an AI system is also a moral choice because it ranks responses and shapes learning. Successful training may show that the system follows this ranking, but not that it is justified or should govern every case. This article uses normative-conceptual analysis to examine how ethical frameworks become AI objectives and which moral, interpretive, epistemic, and institutional judgments that conversion requires. It compares consequentialist, Kantian, virtue-based and contractualist approaches, then uses Theravāda Abhidhamma as a hard case because its fine-grained ethical structure makes the translation problem especially visible. The analysis identifies seven bridge judgments concerning what is evaluated, how ethical categories apply to a machine, what evidence supports that application, how considerations are compared, where the objective applies, whose interpretation governs and when revision is required. Because no ethical source settles all seven, technical success cannot make a reward morally final. The article develops reward finalism and the moral finality gap, derives a principle of reward non-finality, and proposes a seven-question audit for making the judgments behind alignment claims explicit and treating rewards in open-ended settings as non-final specifications open to challenge and revision.

items.title: Russellian Physicalism and the Mereological Role of Categorical Properties.
items.abstract: I develop a new account of the metaphysical role of categorical properties within Russellian physicalism. After defining Russellian monism, I focus on Brown’s determination role, on which fundamental categorical properties fix the higher-level categorical character of objects. I argue that Russellian physicalists have reason to assign categorical properties a further and explanatorily prior role of grounding mereological composition, in virtue of which certain pluralities count as proper wholes rather than mere aggregates, offering a distinctive response to the question of what makes genuine composites exist in the first place. On this view, the categorical basis of reality fixes which proper wholes exist at all. Even if Brown’s determination role and the proposed mereological role are co-extensive, this does not amount to identity, and any analysis of Russellian physicalism will be incomplete if it does not address its implicit mereological assumptions. I consider a conceivability-based argument to explore how the mereological role differs from the determination role. Moreover, I claim that the mereological role can help address the swapped inscrutables objection and other common challenges to Russellian physicalism in a more robust manner. Integrating both roles yields a more complete Russellian physicalism, on which the same metaphysical mechanism that grounds mereological unity also grounds consciousness.

items.title: The Set Structure of Concepts: A Methodological Turn from Synchronic Analysis to Diachronic Construction.
items.abstract: Traditional concept analysis often presupposes that the world itself contains classifications, seeking objective and exhaustive distinguishing features. This ontological obsession leads to circular definitions when dealing with complex concepts such as life and mind. This paper proposes a turn from ontology to epistemology: concepts are not objective mappings of the world in itself, but rather information compression and structural classification adopted by humans under limited cognitive capacity. Every concept inherently corresponds to an object set O and a feature set F. The order of their occurrence is that the object set O precedes the feature set F; that is, the determining order is O → F. The essence of definition is to further compress information and thereby produce structural classification through the genus concept and features in genus. Defining concepts by concepts necessarily confronts three possible trajectories in its logical structure: infinite iteration, circular definition, or the choice of termination. Due to limited cognitive resources, infinite iteration is unfeasible; because definition demands clarity, circular definition is untenable. Therefore, the chain of definition can ultimately only terminate at "primordial concepts" that can no longer be formally defined. Given the intractability of complex conceptual networks at the synchronic level, this paper argues that the method must shift from "analysis" to "construction." For the continuity of construction, this paper divides concepts into two categories. The first category of concepts lacks a network structure and possesses synchronic reproducibility; they can be constructed through analytic reduction and reproduction at present. The second category of concepts forms a network structure around life, and the process through which the structure of their real-world objects evolves cannot be synchronically reproduced; therefore, they must turn to a diachronic path. Taking "life" itself as the primordial concept, and combining first-category concepts from the simple to the complex through life-history deduction, their evolutionary process is reenacted. This methodological turn provides a genetic reconstruction path for the clarification and precision of practical philosophy.

items.title: AI Is Not Authentic and Does Not Know Its Position: A Response to Apple's The Illusion of Thinking.
items.abstract: Apple's The Illusion of Thinking, published in June 2025, reports that frontier reasoning models, when tested on controlled puzzles, suffer from accuracy collapse, a counterintuitive decline in reasoning effort, overthinking and premature commitment to early errors, and an inability to use explicit algorithms. This paper does only one thing: it lists the problems. Section I sets out the problems identified in Apple's paper, Section II sets out the problems with Apple's own method, and Section III presents this paper's new insight, AI Is Not Authentic and Does Not Know Its Position. The paper stops there; it offers no method.

items.title: Practical Entrustment in AI-Mediated Inquiry – from Epistemic Infrastructure to Epistemic Friction.
items.abstract: This study introduces the notion of practical entrustment (a-ffidarsi) to characterize a form of human–artificial intelligence (AI) epistemic dependence that extends beyond the existing trust- and reliance-based frameworks. Rather than replacing those frameworks, a-ffidarsi identifies a distinct level of analysis: the stabilization of an AI system’s operations of selection, framing, and task articulation as operative background conditions for epistemic activity, without being individuated by whatever attitude the agent holds toward the system or its outputs. Drawing on Heidegger’s account of Zuhandenheit, Merleau-Ponty’s analysis of motor intentionality, and Dreyfus’s reconstruction of skilled coping, the analysis characterizes a-ffidarsi, in its paradigmatic form, as a structural transformation of the intentional field distinguished by the infrastructural position AI mediation occupies relative to epistemic evaluation. This account explains how AI systems can acquire epistemic authority by shaping the field within which evaluation, endorsement, trust, distrust, and scrutiny subsequently operate. The analysis then examines the normative implications of this infrastructural role through the principle of epistemic friction preservation and the upstream redistribution of responsibility. The resulting framework provides a basis for evaluating design and institutional adoption choices that make AI epistemically infrastructural while preserving the conditions for contestability and deliberate epistemic agency.

items.title: Who is to Blame? A Polemic on Legacy.
items.abstract: The following is a short polemic on who deserves blame for their legacy. There are two main camps: one maintains that a figure is not responsible for the environment they cultivate; another asserts the radical position that the figure deserves everything that is possibly connected to them. Both camps are wrong, and while there is no central answer to the ethical question of one’s legacy, there is a responsible method for arriving at a solid answer tailored to a specific case. It involves an attention to details and a close historical eye.

items.title: Uma investigação sobre a posição epistêmica do sábio.
items.pub: Dissertation, Federal University of Santa Catarina
items.abstract: This dissertation investigates the epistemic standing that grounds the figure of the wise person. Starting from the analysis of historical paradigms and the stipulation of conceptual desiderata, such as the impossibility of transmission via testimony, the accommodation of human fallibility, the need for diachronic evaluation, and the explanation of the capacity to advise, the study critically evaluates the three main alternatives in contemporary epistemology: knowledge, justified belief, and understanding. First, it rejects the reduction of wisdom to a form of propositional knowledge, focusing the critique on Stephen Grimm's proposal. It is demonstrated that this approach faces a structural dilemma: it is too weak, as it allows wisdom to be theoretically acquired through the mere acceptance of testimony, and excessively restrictive, since its factivist condition (the commitment to truth) excludes from the set of sages paradigmatic figures from Antiquity who were subject to environmental epistemic luck and superseded scientific theories. Next, the study contests the alternative of justified belief, expressed in Sharon Ryan's Deep Rationality Theory (DRT). It is argued that, besides the fact that evidentialist rigor does not prevent morally reprehensible deliberations from being rationally justified, the proposal rests on a strictly synchronic methodological assumption. Drawing on virtue theory, it becomes evident that evaluations based on isolated temporal snapshots are inadequate to capture the historical cultivation, narrative agency, and diachronic habituation of the intellectual virtues inherent to wisdom. As a solution to these impasses, it is defended that objectual understanding constitutes the true epistemic standing of wisdom. Because it requires the agent's cognitive control and the holistic grasp of networks of explanatory relations, understanding demands an untransferable personal effort, not being susceptible to testimonial delegation. By adopting a non-factivist perspective, the theory manages to accommodate the possession of peripheral false beliefs by historical sages, while the dispositional skills of cognitive control enable counterfactual testing and the diachronic gradation of intellectual character. Finally, the research applies this thesis to the practical act of advising, rejecting its assimilation to constative acts of testimony. Good advice is defined as a performative speech act of a directive nature that operates as an epistemic …

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework in Its Own Terms: An Empirical Synthesis of Rigidity, Release and Practice.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) describes ten inner powers that everyone has, grouped in the Head, Heart and Gut, none good or bad in itself. Distress arises from emotional rigidity, when a few powers fuse and suppress the rest; the remedy is practice, including Emotional Cycling. After a claim-by-claim audit of the empirical work so far, this synthesis counts only tests of relations the framework itself states. Earlier negative verdicts that rested on the analysts’ interpretations, including the first article’s findings on trait scales, centres and counter-poles and six results of the second article, are withdrawn as evidence about the framework. Eight results bear on its stated claims. Four were supported: in other teams’ daily-life data, being caught up in one’s thoughts went with negative feeling (r = .46) and depressive symptoms (ρ = .66), and acceptance and confidence each added to happiness; and clarity about a personal situation rose after reading about CEF (dz = .39; no control group). Two were mixed and two not supported. Descriptively, dominance appeared as a matter of degree, not fixed types, and 72% of pilot participants had at least one power easy to ignite but hard to release. Research by others on defusion, acceptance and flexibility is consistent with the framework. Its central practice remains untested; a randomised study is proposed. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; emotional rigidity; cognitive fusion; acceptance; Emotional Cycling; psychological flexibility; self-reported clarity; experience sampling; claim audit; exploratory synthesis.

items.title: Building an AI-Powered Innovation Wormhole: Transferring Solutions Across Industries Instead of Reinventing Them.
items.abstract: Innovation effort is frequently spent solving problems that have already been addressed elsewhere, because solutions remain confined within organizational, industrial, scientific, linguistic, and geographical boundaries. This paper develops the AI Innovation Wormhole, a mechanism-centered, AI-mediated framework for discovering, reconstructing, evaluating, adapting, and validating problem-solving mechanisms across disconnected organizations, startups, industries, research communities, and innovation ecosystems. The framework's unit of transfer is not a document, product, or isolated idea, but a problem-solving mechanism: a typed configuration of entities, activities, relations, constraints, and enabling conditions, represented together with the evidence supporting it. The paper formalizes mechanisms as typed attributed hypergraphs with evidence links, defines structural correspondence as a typed graph-alignment problem, and specifies a transfer pipeline comprising problem representation, mechanism discovery, reconstruction, correspondence analysis, transferability assessment, adaptation design, target-domain validation, and provenance tracking. It distinguishes three epistemic states — candidate transfer, justified transfer hypothesis, and validated transfer — and situates the framework relative to analogical reasoning, case-based reasoning, TRIZ-based function-oriented search, literature-based discovery, and causal transportability theory. The paper identifies failure modes, governance requirements, and evaluation metrics, and proposes a staged research program with falsifiable propositions. Its narrower, testable claim is that a systematic, mechanism-centered approach can reveal useful cross-domain connections that conventional retrieval, classification, and similarity-based recommendation fail to expose.

items.title: Equilibrated paradox: A phenomenological study of subject-object consciousness in anorexia nervosa.
Replacement Economics in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: Arti cial intelligence may change the relationship among production, employment, and the distribution of income. If AI systems come to replace human labor across a broad range of occupations, the problem that follows goes beyond temporary unemployment and occupational retraining: when employment income is no longer reliable, can people still obtain, on a continuing basis, the material resources needed to sustain an acceptable standard of living? Existing institutions provide several buers against technological change. Markets reallocate labor and capital; education and retraining facilitate occupational transitions; monetary and scal policy aect aggregate demand and investment; taxes and transfers redistribute income; social insurance protects against particular risks. These mechanisms remain important. This paper asks whether, under su ciently broad and persistent replacement of labor, their present forms and combinations can secure a social minimum. It proposes Replacement Economics in the Age of AI as a research program and oers a conditional argument built around the household-level gap. The argument has three steps: it examines the limits of each existing adjustment mechanism; it identi es the conditions under which technological replacement leaves a structural gap between available resources and the resources that a social minimum requires; and, where such a gap exists, it compares possible institutional arrangements, in particular the distribution of the wealth that AI creates and broad participation in productive assets and their returns. The paper does not predict whether large-scale replacement will occur. It is conditional on the degree of replacement, and takes the loss of 70%80% of the preAI wage bill to net replacement as a stress scenario for testing institutional resilience. The central question is whether institutions can secure basic living conditions when the traditional link between human labor and personal income is substantially weakened.

items.title: Doing philosophy with fictions and games: a regulatory account of bracketed engagement.
К философии вымирания человечества: математический подход.
items.abstract: В этой книге исследуется вопрос о том, приближается ли Homo sapiens к условиям, угрожающим его долгосрочному выживанию, и задается вопрос о том, как исследовать эту возможность, не смешивая культурные представления, научные данные и математические предположения. Начинается книга с разграничения биологического вымирания от апокалиптических нарративов, спекулятивной фантастики, псевдонаучных утверждений и краха цивилизации. Затем рассматривается этот вид во взаимозависимом контексте планетных систем, технологического развития, социальной организации и человеческого поведения. В исследовании предлагается использовать Математическую матрицу жизнеспособности Homo sapiens (MMV-HS) в качестве основы для описания взаимодействующих факторов давления, путей катастрофического риска, вероятностей выживания и условий восстановления. Модель представлена как исследовательская архитектура, а не как калиброванный прогноз: иллюстративные расчеты не могут установить вероятность вымирания человечества без обоснованных эмпирических параметров и явного учета неопределенности. Полученная оценка отвергает как заверения в неизбежном прогрессе, так и утверждения о надвигающемся биологическом вымирании. Жизнеспособность человечества, напротив, предстает как условная, динамическая проблема, исследование которой должно отличать выживание видов от цивилизационной преемственности и адаптивной способности. Философский вывод намеренно открыт: признание ограничений прогнозирования не уменьшает значимости доказательств, предотвращения, институциональной ответственности или коллективного выбора. Ключевые слова: вымирание человечества; экзистенциальный риск; жизнеспособность видов; модели выживания; неопределенность; философия науки. -/- .

items.title: Glossa tenebrosa: A Diary on Holding.
items.abstract: In 1888, a Russian physician at Charcot's clinic pays three francs for a Latin treatise condemned by the Inquisition in 1516. He sets out to diagnose its author. Then he falls ill, and something dark and sweet takes up residence in his heart. Over twenty-seven years, his diary pursues one question through medicine, scripture, and the occult: who holds a life together, and can a man hold himself?

items.title: What Counts as a Philosophical Position? Thesis, Commitment, Attribution, and the Limits of Doctrinal Labels.
items.abstract: Philosophical reference works often record a person, school, or tradition as holding a named position: realism, empiricism, skepticism, compatibilism, nihilism, or virtue ethics. Yet a label may denote a specific thesis, a family of related theses, a method of inquiry, a practical orientation, or an interpretation imposed by later commentators. A philosopher may assert an argument's premise without endorsing it, explore a hypothesis without accepting it, deny a false dichotomy, or suspend judgment. If these distinctions are erased, maps of philosophy turn apparent similarities into invented agreement and differences of vocabulary into invented disagreement. -/- This paper develops the Attributed Position Account (APA-10), a ten-field framework for representing a philosophical position as an issue-relative, force-sensitive, source-grounded, and defeasible commitment profile. It separates a thesis's propositional content from the subject's attitude toward it, distinguishes the scope and domain of a claim from the label applied to it, records inferential obligations and potential defeaters, and grades the evidence for attribution. A five-gate Position Attribution Test (PAT) helps researchers determine whether a source supports explicit endorsement, qualified commitment, methodological posture, suspension, a later reconstruction, or only a thematic association. -/- Eight analytical cases examine ontological commitment, scientific realism and constructive empiricism, the analysis of knowledge, logical pluralism, ethical outlooks, Pyrrhonian suspension, Madhyamaka emptiness, and culturally situated intellectual traditions. Two negative controls show why Madhyamaka is not simply nihilism and why suspension is not denial. A compact formal model demonstrates how opposite verdicts can result from changing a claim's quantifier, domain, epistemic force, or attribution basis while retaining the same popular label. -/- The paper extends the author's original distinction among philosophical questions, positions, and traditions in The Coordinates of Thought — Philosophy: Every Question, Answer, Thinker and Tradition (2026) and its companion philosophical reference platform. It follows the previous three papers in the Philosophy Mapping and Disagreement Series while grounding its philosophical claims in separately identified primary texts and scholarly literature. -/- Supplementary materials include the APA-10 codebook, an attribution worksheet, eight constructed …

items.title: The Nuremberg Chronicle 1493: Sources.
items.abstract: Literature sources and references for the Nuremberg Chronicle, fol. Ir to VIIr. In addition a contemporary German (and English) translation is presented from comparing the existing Latin, Early New High German and English (translation) texts for better comprehensibility.

items.title: Tragédia, Loteria e Abismo: os mitos do moralismo católico.
items.abstract: A investigação contemporânea em filosofia analítica da ação, epistemologia e ética normativa, fortemente marcada pelas contribuições de Bernard Williams, Thomas Nagel, Gideon Rosen, e pelos debates sobre agência, contingência e moral luck, convidam a uma revisão radical das pretensões sistemáticas da teologia moral católica, tal qual estampada no Catecismo Oficial. A exposição dogmática contida no Catecismo da Igreja Católica (CIC), especialmente nos parágrafos dedicados à dignidade humana, à liberdade, às fontes da moralidade e ao pecado (CIC 1699-1874), apresenta-se, em seus próprios termos, como um bloco normativo que é erguido pelo pensamento católico com base na simetria e no entrelace entre a "ordem divina", a "consciência" e a responsabilidade subjetiva. Contudo, a abertura da razão filosófica aos desenvolvimentos recentes no campo, traz a oportunidade de identificarmos e "isolarmos" profundas fendas e rachaduras naquilo que, a um olhar superficial, é um monolito impassível.

items.title: Love, Money, and Blame.
Natural Possibility 48 The Human Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper 48, investigates the development of human intelligence and the possibility that certain educational, social, and intellectual structures may unnecessarily restrict its wider capabilities. Within the Natural Possibility framework, it examines relationships between independent thinking, physical experience, curiosity, knowledge, and the conditions through which understanding develops. Particular attention is given to childhood education, the influence of different learning environments, and the distinction between accumulating information and developing the ability to organise, connect, and apply it. The investigation also considers interdisciplinary understanding, the relationship between human intelligence and artificial intelligence, and the importance of maintaining intellectual independence. Drawing upon earlier Natural Possibility investigations, the paper introduces further philosophical questions concerning the potential development and purpose of human intelligence beyond currently established understanding. Rather than presenting definitive conclusions, it identifies possibilities for educational improvement, intellectual development, and future investigation into the relationships between mind, knowledge, experience, and reality.

items.title: World Models Without Worlds II: Why Learned Models Do Not Refer, and Why Guardrails and Validation Cannot Close the Gap.
items.abstract: Since 2025 the phrase "world model" has come to name at least six architectures: latent predictors in the JEPA line, generative video simulators, explicit spatial generators, model-based agents, evaluation simulators for autonomous driving, and hybrids in which a language model directs a generator. This paper asks one question of every architecture, which I call the entry audit: when a predicted continuation can be read in two ways that call for different actions, what in the system selects the reading, and where did the selector come from? Drawing on the builders' own technical reports and on independent evaluations of their systems, it finds in every case a locatable import: curated data, probes trained on human labels, goal images, rewards derived from annotation, supplied camera frames, game engines, logged trajectories, or a language model. Part I sets out the general argument: the fibres of the observation map; the selection of data; the probe as the fixing of a gauge that identifiability theory leaves free; the difference between prediction and state; and the supplied goal. It proves what I call the hybrid paradox: a certified architecture never admits an action whose safety depends on a distinction its formal layer does not itself draw, so that a formal layer able to draw every such distinction would make the learned layer redundant for safety, while a learned layer that could be formally controlled would, for safety, be a formal layer under another name. It then shows, with a recent finite-testing result and a direct argument from underdetermination, why no campaign of tests in a simulator yields a bound, free of assumptions about the distribution the system will meet, on the cases in which simulator and world come apart, and that the tested cases are themselves a selection whose remainder no score measures. Part II audits each family through the achievements its builders report, among them an agent that learns from recorded play alone to mine iron in Minecraft and a driving simulator validated at three separate levels against real outcomes, conceding those achievements. Part III records what the variations change, proposes an ambiguity test that would discriminate between the claims, and states a falsifiable re-absorption prediction. The variations move the point at which meaning enters, so that it arrives in one family with the data and in another with the goal or the language model, and none of them removes that point.

items.title: Before the Field Closes: TEN VIRTUES TO LIVE BEFORE DEATH.
items.abstract: Which virtues must a person have actually lived before death closes the field of their own acts? The Philosophy of Virtues forbids the obvious answer, a ranking with Freedom at the top, because freedom is the element of every virtue rather than one of them. This paper replaces the ranking with a selection operator, the Closure Filter. It admits a virtue only if the virtue (C1) can be lived only in the first person, (C2) leaves an irreparable omission when unexercised at death, and (C3) can be begun by an act on an available occasion rather than arriving as a by-product. Run on all 111 virtues of the programme's catalogue, the 101 of the Filosofia das Virtudes and ten cross-traditional candidates, the filter admits thirty-one. The degeneracy test groups them into ten: Free Will, Honesty, Courage, Love, Family, Purpose, Forgiveness and Restitution, Gratitude, Joy, and the Unveiling lived as wonder. Wisdom, Serenity and Equanimity are excluded as fruits rather than tasks. The civic virtues, distributive justice and the Virtue of Protection are excluded as conditions for other people's lives rather than first-person experiences; justice in one's own dealings is admitted. Priority is conceded to Aristotle on the complete life, to Tolstoy, to Heidegger on death as the call back from living as "one" lives, to Kierkegaard and Sartre, to Erikson on generativity, to Byock's four things that matter most, and to Carstensen's socioemotional selectivity theory. What remains is a test that separates a virtue lived from a virtue displayed, and a conjecture about the mechanism of self-deception: the more faithful the display, the later its own author discovers it. One prediction is registered with its falsifier. The selection is single-coder and carries no evidential weight. Claims about the wellbeing of dying persons are a speculative extension outside the programme's competence. The result bears directly on what freedom and the virtues mean for human beings now. A virtue is freedom exercised in a domain of life, so a person who has not authored their own acts has not lived any virtue, however perfectly they display it. Social credit systems, platform metrics and AI systems trained on displayed conduct can reward the appearance of every one of these ten virtues. None of them can live a single one on a person's behalf. Protecting the freedom in which the ten can be lived is therefore not one political good among others. It is the condition of a human life that its owner …

items.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Participate in Ritual? From Ritual Mediation to Religious Authority: Agency, Attribution, and Legitimate Authorization.
items.abstract: Generative AI has entered settings such as prayer aids, question-answering systems for religious texts, synthetic saintly personas, and spiritual care. Yet a system’s influence on ritual does not mean that users recognize it as an authority; user trust is not equivalent to communal authorization; and institutional authorization does not necessarily resolve internal contestation. This article asks a narrower, testable question: How does AI move from technical mediation within ritual to religious authority with de facto normative force? Through a critical synthesis of the literature and comparative case analysis, it engages 2026 research on generative charisma, infrastructures for scriptural interpretation, Buddhist AI roles, religious-organization governance, and Muslim users’ experiences. It does not claim to originate a theory of AI religious authority or to establish the five roles as a new universal taxonomy. Instead, it treats tool, guide, interpreter, participant, and authority as action positions that can shift or coexist within a ritual event, and diagnoses each event along four non-interchangeable dimensions: technical causal influence, attribution of authority, de facto normative efficacy, and institutional authorization together with claims to legitimacy (the fact of authorization need not be universally recognized). Knowledge compression, relational substitution, and normative closure are treated as potentially reinforcing mechanisms, not as verified causal laws. Comparative cases suggest that generative charisma, data provenance, and institutional framing may give AI recommendations practical force, although the strength of evidence varies across studies. The article’s narrower contribution is to operationalize existing work on authority, power, and authorization in a comparative matrix for ritual events. The matrix asks who initiates interaction, supplies interpretation, recognizes its efficacy, can refuse, and bears the consequences, and translates these questions into governance requirements concerning authorization scope, responsibility, appeals, and withdrawal. The article argues that AI religious authority is not a natural extension of model capability, but a sociotechnical relation among technical configuration, user acceptance, institutional authorization, and procedures for contestation—elements that may align or conflict.

items.title: From Training to Retained Capability: Lightweight AI, Maintainability and Evidence Standards in China–Africa Digital Cooperation.
items.abstract: China–Africa digital cooperation is frequently assessed through infrastructure outputs and training quotas, yet the conversion of these inputs into durable local capabilities remains poorly evidenced. This article examines China–Africa artificial intelligence cooperation, as it bears on African Union continental frameworks up to 2025, through the lens of development politics and digital sovereignty. It proposes Lightweight AI not merely as a technical specification but as a sociotechnical proportionality principle encompassing language, energy, maintenance, governance and exit conditions. Applying a structured evidence-ladder methodology to continental policy texts, ITU digital-development evidence, and symmetric comparator programmes (World Bank DE4A, GIZ FAIR Forward), the study finds a structural asymmetry: regional commitments to capability and inclusion are robust, while public evidence regarding knowledge retention and institutional ownership remains thin—a gap that reflects a broader industry-wide failure in capacity-building evaluation rather than a uniquely bilateral defect. To address this, the article operationalises a twelve-indicator Cybersophy framework and introduces a seven-dimension maintainability boundary and a capability-retention ledger. Applying these tools to the Luban Workshop initiative reveals the specific evidentiary voids between activity delivery and autonomous operation. The article argues that under heterogeneous material constraints, lightweight design and rigorous retention tracking constitute institutional commitments to safeguarding human agency, offering a new evidence standard for evaluating technology transfer in the global South.

items.title: The Project View and the Phenomenology of Partiality.
items.abstract: Can our projects explain why we act partially toward specific individuals? I defend the project view of partiality against the objection that it cannot capture the role of personal identity in motivating partial action. Simon Keller (2013) argues that ground projects fail to explain how information about specific persons shapes an actor's motivating reasons. I show that this objection fails on two levels: (1) interpersonal ground projects constitutively include information about specific individuals, and (2) motivating reasons can be fully specified by ground projects even when the actor is not aware of the identity of the person in question. This means that the project view remains a plausible account of partiality.

items.title: Open Letter to Thinkers: the Objective Value of the Subjective.
items.abstract: This note brings to attention the minimal mathematical complexity of generic thought and thinkers. It is argued that independent thought has objective value.

items.title: On knowing a person: a phenomenological account.
items.abstract: This article sets out a phenomenological account of the experience of knowing a particular person. By this I do not mean knowledge claims rooted in generalised trait ascriptions or culturally scripted self-narratives, but how we know a person as a singular manifestation and an irreplaceable presence. While existentially and socially significant, this experience remains surprisingly underexplored. I argue that knowing a person in this respect is a matter of familiarity with that person’s particular presence as a living gestalt. I begin by delimiting the phenomenon on ontological and epistemological grounds, arguing that the concept of a living gestalt offers us a way of understanding phenomena that are at once individual, evolving and open to experience. On this basis, I propose a phenomenological account of how we come to know a person as a living gestalt through three registers, and of how familiarity is inflected by the depth of reciprocity in the relation. The registers are: (1) embodied sensorium and existential style; (2) instituting a world; and (3) “living-in”. To make otherwise tacit experiential dimensions salient, I illustrate each register with the contrasting experience of forgetting a person. I conclude by examining the limits of imitation in the context of the digital resurrection debate, arguing that the three registers constitute fundamental obstacles to any genuine replacement of a person’s singular presence at the experiential level.

items.title: The Kripke-Miller puzzle.
items.abstract: In Naming and Necessity Kripke called his causal theory of reference a mere ‘picture’, citing the difficulty of finding the necessary and sufficient conditions for reference. To illustrate the difficulty he presented an obscure puzzle as to why a name of a famous person and a name of an unfamous person seem to have different conditions for reference transmission. This paper argues that the puzzle concerns a pragmatic phenomenon of reference and is irrelevant to the question of what conditions are necessary and sufficient for transmission of a semantic reference. To that end, a notion of ‘hearer’s reference’ is introduced in contrast to the notions of semantic reference and speaker’s reference, and then a solution to the puzzle is provided in terms of hearer’s reference.

items.title: Метанаука аномалий: влияние сознания на материю. Приложение КНИГИ XII Смысловые поля серии "Законы управления психо-историей" Автор : Ю.Л. Зорин.
items.abstract: Приложение к Книге XII серии «Законы управления психо-историей» представляет собой исследовательскую программу, расширяющую операторно-спектральный формализм смысловых полей на класс явлений, традиционно относимых к области аномалий. -/- В работе вводится понятие метанауки как обобщения классической науки на классы условий и свойств. На этой основе формулируется концепция воспроизводимости на классах, позволяющая анализировать эффекты, которые не воспроизводятся буквально при копировании протоколов, но демонстрируют устойчивые закономерности при определённых конфигурациях системы «оператор — установка». -/- Центральным элементом модели выступает параметр согласованности \(\Coh(t)\) — количественная мера структурной согласованности состояния сознания (психики) оператора и физической системы.
