Вводятся операторы синхронизации \(\IMsync\) и актуализации \(\IMact\), с помощью которых описывается гипотетическое влияние состояния наблюдателя на динамику физических процессов. -/- Рассматриваются следующие тестовые классы явлений: низкоэнергетические ядерные реакции и холодный ядерный синтез; биологические трансмутации элементов; сообщения о дополнительном энергетическом канале (включая гипотезы энергии физического вакуума); предельные случаи («внутреннее питание» и подобные). -/- Для каждой гипотезы явно сформулированы критерии фальсификации. Показано, как операторный фактор сознания может быть включён в математическое описание без нарушения принципа научной проверяемости. -/- Приложение также содержит вспомогательные гипотезы (обобщенная схема 3-х мерной периодической системы элементов, космогонический сценарий возникновения жизни, концентрация распределённых потоков энергии), демонстрирующие возможности формализма за пределами основной предметной области. -/- Работа носит характер исследовательской программы. Все предложенные конструкции отделены от эмпирически подтверждённого знания и предназначены для последующей экспериментальной проверки. -/- Книга адресована исследователям, работающим на стыке физики, психофизиологии, теории сложных систем и методологии науки, а также читателям, интересующимся строгим формальным подходом к проблеме влияния сознания на материальные процессы.

items.title: Intensionalism and Triviality.
items.abstract: Given the intensionalism that Timothy Williamson defends in Overfitting and Heu-ristics in Philosophy and elsewhere, necessarily equivalent propositions are identical. This threatens to trivialize metaphysics and other areas of inquiry focused on what is necessary. Williamson addresses this threat, appealing to the fact that we believe propositions under guises. I here distinguish between two versions of the triviality threat. One is epistemic and one metaphysical. I argue that Williamson deals only with the epistemic threat. I also discuss various strategies for responding to the met-aphysical threat.

items.title: The Field Before the Point of View: Korsgaard and the Order of Normative Reception.
items.abstract: Christine Korsgaard holds that normativity is not found in the world but brought to it by practical reason. O amanhã é possível? defends the reverse order: the position of those who participate in a common condition bears on action before any agent recognizes it, and practical reason receives what the field already contained. The question examined is whether conditions of participation can ground reasons to be answerable to others independently of recognition, complaint, or actual interaction. An argumentative axis of Korsgaard's work between 1992 and 2018 is reconstructed: obligation established through address and reciprocity, in the Tanner Lectures; public reasons grounded in interaction, in Self-Constitution; intersubjective value, in Creating the Kingdom of Ends; the good tethered to a creature with a point of view and the relational identification of the future addressees of duties, in Fellow Creatures. It is shown, first, that the analysis of the constitutive, which Korsgaard applies to the agent's own activity, can be applied to other people's forms of participation, and that classifying a reason as external depends on the description chosen. It is then shown that Korsgaard herself admits reasons prior to reflective recognition and builds value from something received, so that the disagreement narrows to the authority of a demand over another agent. The case of someone who alters an archive in an empty room is developed with an explicit normative premise and serves to formulate the question whether address constitutes that authority or makes it perceptible. Three objections of Korsgaardian inspiration, concerning method, realism, and perspectivedependence, are examined. The difference between the two proposals is found to lie in grounding, not necessarily in obligations. Korsgaard already identifies relationally the addressees of duties to future generations; the normativity of participation proposes to specify that relation as participation in common conditions, and its possible advantage, indicated but not yet demonstrated, would lie in bringing under a single criterion the present inhabitants of a condition and the future occupants of the positions it distributes.

items.title: Minds and Machines - A course in the philosophy of mind and AI. Course support, 2026.
items.abstract: This is the course support „Minds and Machines”, taught at the Mind the Brain Master, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Bucharest by Marian Călborean, in late 2026. It is published as open educational resource under CC BY 4.0 license, which allows re-use with attribution. The course is a focused and revised selection of themes established in the previous course "Filosofia computației: Realitate și calcul, 2026" (in Romanian, available on Philpapers/Figshare). -/- Starting from the foundations of computing, this course examines how increasingly capable AI systems can be characterized reliably and their implications for traditional philosophical concepts. For this, a distinction is maintained between mathematical results, empirical evidence and philosophical hypotheses. After an introductory lecture, it comprises three modules and twelve sessions, the last eight being dedicated to student research: a) Module A: Machine. Four instructor-led lectures establish common foundations. We introduce Turing machines and the Church-Turing thesis (C1), universal computation, the abstract-concrete problem of software, and the limits of computing (C2). Then machine learning, intelligence, and the problem of generalization (C3) precede a history of the engineering of current LLM systems which concludes with the hypothesis of superintelligence with weak identity (C4): AI may acquire extraordinary features while having disjoint numerical, functional, and moral identity. b) Module B: Mind. Four student research sessions revisit classical philosophical positions versus recent AI developments linked to one of Bowman’s 2023 points. We revisit Dreyfus (via AI scaling), Dennett (via emergence), Searle (via AI representations), and Turing (via benchmarks and superintelligence). c) Module C: Agents. Four further student research sessions revisit Leibniz (via AI interpretability), Wiener (via alignment and control), Winner (via values in technology), and Weizenbaum (via human-AI interactions). Having started with the theoretical foundations of computing and after examining the implementation of faculties associated with the human mind in computers, this module explores the interactions of AI with the human world. -/- The entire course follows a flipped-classroom model (advance readings, prepared questions, collective discussion). Students are encouraged to disagree, engage in debates, and develop their own justified philosophical stand.

items.title: Philotechnology: From Ontological Intuition to GLCE V38.
items.abstract: Philotechnology, formulated by Pedro Cervelleira de Mello, is examined as an epistemological apparatus for converting abstract philosophical distinctions into explicit, testable operations. We give the apparatus a retrospective six-stage specification: (1) conceptual distinction, (2) operational constraint, (3) typed mathematical operator, (4) prediction and invariant, (5) independent comparison or ablation, and (6) critical revision or suspension. The General Law of Cosmic Evolution (GLCE) is the worked case, not an independently verified universal law. The documented progression from an unstable matrix recurrence to conservative graph exchange, metric Poisson coupling, local Conatus reservoirs, and V38 dynamic contrast supplies a traceable record of computational construction and failure. In a reused-seed synthetic particle-mesh cosmology benchmark with equal 30,000-edge budgets, V38 achieved 71.03% spatial top-quintile Jaccard versus 68.88% for V36 local Conatus and 65.14% for a sparse fixed network; spectral-shape error was 0.468 dex versus 0.497 dex for V36. In a separate observational audit, a frozen V38-inspired planar adapter reached 54.84% mean edge Jaccard across 86 experimental configurations and 850 final Physarum networks, below both a Tero-family implementation at 58.82% and the unlearned initial geometric network at 56.19% (adapter vs initial: Δ = −1.35 pp, descriptive 95% CI [−2.36, −0.33]; adapter vs Tero: Δ = −3.98 pp, descriptive 95% CI [−5.03, −2.94]). Retrospective ablations did not demonstrate a stable positive biological contribution from either dynamic contrast or Conatus. The original V38 was not executed literally on these biological networks: specimen-matched initial states and physical flow variables were absent. We demonstrate the feasibility of constructing an auditable translation chain and explicit rules for failure and suspension, not the generality, comparative superiority, or cognitive efficacy of Philotechnology. The scope of reality’s mathematical modelability remains an open research question. Keywords: Philotechnology; epistemological protocol; computational philosophy; ontological operationalization; adaptive graphs; GLCE V38; dynamic contradiction; Conatus; synthetic cosmology; Physarum polycephalum; Jaccard similarity; falsifiability.

items.title: Emotional Rigidity and the Practice of Core Emotions: What the Core Emotion Framework Claims and What the Evidence Shows.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) holds that every person has ten basic inner powers (three each in the Head and Heart, four in the Gut), that none is good or bad in itself, that everyday feelings are recipes of several powers, and that distress arises from emotional rigidity: a few powers fuse, dominate and suppress the rest. Its remedy is practice: igniting and releasing each power separately and waking the neglected ones. This paper states these claims in the framework’s terms and reports exploratory tests on de-identified CEF survey data (N = 82 to 822) and three open daily-life datasets (about 2,800 people). Predictions and pass rules were time-stamped before analysis but not registered publicly; p-values were Holm-corrected. Six tests examine relations the author states. Four were supported: being caught up in one’s thoughts went with negative feeling (r = .46) and depressive symptoms (ρ = .66); acceptance and confidence each added to happiness; and clarity about one’s own problem rose after reading CEF (dz = .39, no control group). One was mixed and one not supported. Six further tests of the analysts’ own readings are moved to an appendix and not counted. Published research on psychological flexibility is broadly consistent with the framework’s core idea. The main claim, that practice increases flexibility, remains untested; a randomised study is proposed. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; emotional rigidity; psychological flexibility; cognitive fusion; emotion regulation; mixed emotions; experience sampling; exploratory analysis.

items.title: The False Hope of Illusionism: Critical Notice of House of Mirrors by François Kammerer. [REVIEW]
The People We Could Have Become: Alternative Selves, Biographical Counterfactuals, Identity, and Regret.
items.abstract: When we imagine how our lives might have unfolded after a different choice, we often alter the events while leaving the person who imagines them largely unchanged. Yet choices can change not only our circumstances but also the conditions under which later choices are made, including the commitments and standards through which a life is evaluated. This paper examines the inferences we may draw from present regret about an unrealized life. Its central claim is that present regret does not, by itself, establish either that the person formed by the alternative history would have endorsed that life or that it would have been better for them. The argument distinguishes psychological, biographical, and evaluative continuity, treating the last as a possible basis for attributing judgments rather than a criterion of numerical identity or a necessary condition of agreement. It also identifies a methodological risk: counterfactual imagination may silently select the branch that preserves the present self or best satisfies present ideals, then present that construction as a determinate account of who we would have become. Informed, defeasible reconstruction remains possible, but it lacks correction by the alternative subject’s testimony and conduct. The paper offers neither a theory of personal identity nor a general account of well-being. It clarifies the limits of speaking for an alternative self from the standpoint of the life actually lived.
